result.explanation:
Correct answer: Multiprocessing

When CPUs are used in parallel, it is called multiprocessing. Multiprocessing is the parallel execution of instructions. If a computer has more than one CPU, it can be used in parallel to execute instructions. For example, a database server can use up to eight processors at the same time to improve performance for data queries.

Multithreading is the sharing of a single CPU between multiple tasks. Multiprogramming is the execution of two or more programs by a single computer. Multitasking is the processing of more than one task at a time.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) Synchronize (SYN) scanning

Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) Synchronize (SYN) scanning sends a single packet to each scanned port with the SYN flag set. This indicates a request to open a new connection. If the scanner receives a response with the SYN and acknowledgment (ACK) flags set, this means that the port is likely open. This is known as "half-open" scanning because the scanner does not reply with an ACK packet.

TCP ACK scanning is a network reconnaissance technique where an attacker sends TCP ACK packets to determine the firewall rules, identifying open and filtered ports without initiating a full connection. Christmas (XMAS) scanning is a stealthy port scanning technique in cybersecurity. The attacker sends TCP packets with the FIN, URG, and PSH flags set, probing for open ports without arousing suspicion. TCP connect scanning is a basic network reconnaissance method where an attacker attempts to establish a full TCP connection with target hosts, determining open ports and services by completing the handshake.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Governance

Governance is how management directs an organization to reduce residual risk to an acceptable level set by senior management. Governance must involve oversight to ensure that the goals set by senior management have been met. When performing security governance, Information Technology (IT) managers need to keep security objectives in alignment with business objectives.

A Business Impact Analysis (BIA) is a systematic process used to evaluate and assess the potential impacts of disruptions or incidents on an organization's critical business functions. It identifies and prioritizes these functions based on their importance to the organization's operations and objectives.

A security assessment is a systematic evaluation of an organization's security posture to identify vulnerabilities, risks, and potential threats. It involves analyzing security controls, policies, procedures, and technical implementations to assess their effectiveness in protecting assets and mitigating security risks.

The trickle-down effect is an economic theory suggesting that benefits given to the wealthy or upper class will eventually trickle down to the lower classes. This theory posits that tax breaks, subsidies, and other advantages for the wealthy will lead to increased investment, job creation, and economic growth, benefiting everyone in society. However, critics argue that this theory often fails to materialize in practice, as wealth concentration among the wealthy may not necessarily result in widespread economic benefits for all segments of society.

A Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) model uses specific roles or group memberships to define the level of access that the associated users will have in the environment. Users are not limited to just one group but can have multiple memberships with different levels of access.

The Mandatory Access Control (MAC) model uses labels that include the classification level applied to the data. There is also a label applied to the user that indicates their clearance level. The Discretionary Access Control (DAC) model has the owner determining user access. The owner has the responsibility of following policy within the business, but they grant access at their discretion.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: The most restrictive rights required by users to complete necessary tasks are enforced.

The least privilege principle is used to ensure that subjects are granted only the privileges they need to perform their work tasks and job functions. This is sometimes confused with the need-to-know principle. Need to know is the principle that a user is only allowed to access the information that they need to perform their job.

The most restrictive rights to ‘run’ the system is not correct because of the word ‘run.’ The ability to ‘complete’ the task is the intention of least privilege.

Both answers that have ‘least restrictive rights’ are wrong because least privilege desires to restrict the users as much as possible. If nothing else, it protects the user because they cannot get into trouble, and the best result is that it protects the company and possibly their customer because the user cannot do more than they are supposed to.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Brute-force attack

A brute-force attack is a method used to guess passwords. The attacker sends random password guesses until all possible guesses have been exhausted. Brute-force attacks use password randomizers, which rely on algorithms to generate all possible password options. The more complex a password, the more time it takes to crack. Brute-force attacks can be extremely time-consuming, depending on the length and complexity of the password being attacked.

Spoofing is a cyberattack technique in which an attacker disguises their identity or masquerades as a trusted source to deceive a person and gain unauthorized access. It can involve IP spoofing, email spoofing, or DNS spoofing to trick victims into disclosing sensitive information or granting access to protected resources.

A dictionary attack is a password-cracking method in which an attacker systematically enters a large list of common words, phrases, or previously breached passwords as potential login credentials to gain unauthorized access to user accounts or systems. It exploits weak passwords and is often used in cybersecurity testing and attacks. 

A rainbow table specifically contains known, common, or cracked credentials or credential hashes. The question does not indicate that a rainbow table is used in the attack and instead indicates that the values are being generated.

When penetration testers are given no information, it is referred to as a zero-knowledge test (black box).

Red-box testing is not a standard term for a type of penetration test.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: A pentester with full knowledge of a network conducts a penetration test

Clear-box (formerly known as white-box, which is racially insensitive) testing involves penetration testers being provided with all knowledge of the network prior to beginning a test. This allows for the quickest test, as the attacker does not have to conduct prior research on their target. Companies may use this test to ensure security while reducing the cost of billable hours.

A penetration tester conducting a test with no knowledge of the network is known as a black-box test. This would require the penetration tester to conduct research similar to an outside attacker, providing a more realistic result in many situations. A penetration test with partial network knowledge is known as a gray-box test. This requires a hybrid approach, as some info is provided by the client and the remaining info is gathered using open-source intelligence.

To help you remember these categories, remember that closed-box (formerly known as black-box, which is racially insensitive) testing is similar to the emptiness of a black hole in space. Clear-box testing is related to transparency, such as glass. None of these options would simulate the oversight of a penetration test.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Provisioning

Configuration management helps to ensure that devices are deployed and maintained in a secure state. These are the main stages of configuration management:

  • Provisioning: Provisioning is the process of setting up a device, including installing the OS and apps and setting configuration settings. During the provisioning process, the device should be hardened, with configuration settings to secure options and disable unnecessary applications, ports, and services.
  • Baselining: Baselining defines a normal state for a device. Deviations from this baseline may introduce vulnerabilities into the system. Often, organizations use images for baselining, which allows them to install the image on a device to immediately set it in a secure, approved state.
  • Automation: Administrators can also use automation to monitor and manage system configurations at scale. Automation can be used to set up a system, monitor systems for deviations from the baseline, and apply changes across the enterprise network.

Deployment is not part of configuration management. 

Group Policy is a common way for Windows administrators to automatically apply a setting to multiple systems.

Proxy servers can only rewrite headers for Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) traffic, whereas Network Address Translation (NAT) can rewrite headers for TCP traffic.

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
4.2 Secure network components
4.3 Implement secure communication channels according to design

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Network Address Translation (NAT) rewrites Internet Protocol (IP) headers but does not create and manage connections on behalf of the client.

Proxy servers differ from Network Address Translation (NAT) because they create and manage connections between the client and the destination server. A proxy server will create a new Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) connection on behalf of the client. The traffic between the client and proxy server and the proxy server and destination server are entirely separate connections from a network perspective. This allows proxy servers to manipulate headers in the upper levels of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model.

NAT does not create a new connection on behalf of the client. NAT rewrites the existing headers when a new connection is made.

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
4.2 Secure network components
4.3 Implement secure communication channels according to design

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Wide Area Network (WAN)

Frame relay is a Wide Area Network (WAN) technology that is used between WAN providers and customers for networks that are spread over a large geographical area. Frame Relay was replaced mostly by Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) which was then mostly replaced by Multi-Protocol Label Switching (MPLS).

WAN technology connects devices across the planet. LANs connect devices within a building. PANs connect users to their very local technology (mobile phones, headsets, wearable technology, etc.) MANs connect technology across a city.

Ethernet is a shared media Local Area Network (LAN) technology. Token ring employs a token-passing mechanism to control which systems can transmit over the network medium. Token ring is a LAN technology. Fiber Distributed Data Interface (FDDI) is a high-speed token-passing technology that employs two rings with traffic flowing in opposite directions and is designed for the Metropolitan Area Network (MAN). Bluetooth, IEEE 802.15, is an example of a Personal Area Network (PAN) technology.

result.prompt: Originally, voice networks were considered to be which of the following?

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
4.2 Secure network components

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Circuit-switched

Voice networks were originally circuit-switched. This meant that when a call was placed from a phone on the traditional network (that can be found in homes that have had a phone number for a very long time) a connection was built and established across the network. Once the path of that connection was established, the telephone call would use that path until the phone call ended. This process happens every time a phone call is established on that type of network.

Packet-switched networks include X.25, Frame Relay, Aysnchronous Transport Mode (ATM), and Multi-Protocol Label System (MPLS), for example. When data is sent across these networks, each packet takes its own path. This is also how ethernet networks operate. Data packets can, therefore, arrive out of order. If the packets (frames or cells) are numbered, they can be placed back in the correct order before delivery to the user. Some protocols will even request a retransmission for any missing packets (frames or cells).

Network-switched is not a term found in networking.

Permanent virtual circuits is a term that describes a connection that is built across voice networks and remains in place, permanently. An example of this was the 'red phone' found on the United States president's desk during the Cold War. It was a connection to the Kremlin to ensure the president had quick access to speak with them.

1.2 Understand and apply security concepts

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Preventative

The main types of security controls include the following:

  • Preventive: Preventive controls are designed to stop an incident from happening, eliminating the potential impacts on the business. Fences, locks, and access controls are examples of preventive controls.
  • Detective: Detective controls help to identify that an incident is occurring. CCTV, audit trails, and honeypots are examples of detective controls.
  • Corrective: Corrective controls fix issues after a security incident. Antimalware that removes an infection or an auto-close arm on a door are examples of corrective controls.
  • Recovery: Recovery controls restore normal operations after an incident to a greater extent than corrective ones. Backups and server clusters are examples of recovery controls.
  • Deterrent: Deterrent controls attempt to discourage an incident from occurring. Corporate policies and security cameras are examples of deterrent controls.
  • Compensating: Compensating controls are used as a replacement when the preferred control is unusable. For example, a company renting an office in a building may put locks on the doors when it can't build a fence.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Fuzz Testing

Application vulnerabilities are a common target for cybercriminals. Some ways to manage the number of vulnerabilities that reach production include:

  • Fuzz Testing: Fuzzing sends various inputs to an application to try to identify failure cases. These inputs may be randomly generated or intelligently selected based on a model of the system to maximize the probability of finding an issue.
  • Code Review: Code review involves another developer reviewing code for potential issues. Often, this is accomplished by requiring a review before code is incorporated into a code repository.
  • Interface Testing: Interface testing verifies that the different components of a system will work properly when linked together. The four types of interfaces to test include APIs, User Interfaces (UIs), network interfaces, and physical interfaces.
  • Misuse Case Testing: Misuse or abuse case testing identifies ways in which a user could misuse an application and tests its responses to these malicious inputs.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Kerberos

Kerberos is a Single Sign-On (SSO) technology that uses symmetric encryption and the concept of tickets to grant access to resources within a realm. Users request tickets from the Key Distribution Center (KDC), and the tickets provided by the KDC are used to authenticate a user when they attempt to access a resource.

Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) is commonly used right now in the cloud as an SSO technology. There is no KDC, but there are tokens created to pass information along regarding someone's authentication. Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) can be used in the authentication process but it is not an SSO technology and there is no KDC. KDC can only be found in Kerberos. Open Identification (OpenID) is another cloud-based SSO technology, but again there is no KDC.

The clipping level is a threshold for the number of error occurrences before it's considered suspicious or sets off an alarm. For example, ten attempts with an incorrect password triggers an account lockout and password reset. This is more commonly referred to as a threshold.

Set how verbose system logs are does not relate to a specific term, such as clipping level. Setting the logging so that the corporation will have all the records it needs is critical.

There is a sender score related to those that send out emails. It allows recipients to determine the trustworthiness of the email (not an instant message) based on that information.

Ranking a vulnerability's criticality is done using the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS). Scores range from 1 to 10, where 10 is the most severe.

During a lunch break, the finance employee uses Wireshark to sniff the traffic of the sales department and obtain session cookie information. With this information, the finance employee uses the stolen credentials to log in as the sales employee. Pricing data is temporarily changed, impacting online orders and resulting in a financial loss for the company. At the surface level, it appears as if the sales employee made a major mistake. What attack MOST LIKELY occurred in this situation?

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Session sidejacking

Session sidejacking occurs when an attacker steals credentials by sniffing the traffic of other users, who are also on the same network as the attacker. In this example, the session cookies derived from the initial authentication of the victim were stolen by the attacker and used for a malicious act.

SQL injection would involve the usage of specially crafted code to receive a response from a server. Credential stuffing does not apply, since the actual credentials of the victim were not obtained or used on various common websites in an attempt to gain additional access on other platforms. Privilege escalation did not occur here, since this attack typically involves moving from one security level to a higher level. In this example, moving from the finance department to sales was not necessarily an escalation in the privilege of a user.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Warm site

Recovery sites can be classified based on the level of infrastructure they provide and the amount of work needed to bring them online. These are the main types:

  • Cold: A cold site provides a location and potentially infrastructure (power, internet, etc.) but no devices. It is the cheapest type of site to maintain but the slowest and most expensive to bring online.
  • Warm: A warm site has more equipment than a cold site. It may include some devices, but others must be added when they become necessary.
  • Hot: A hot site is an exact copy of the primary site with the same devices and the same data (potentially with some lag). It’s the most expensive type of site to maintain but the fastest to use.

Some disaster response groups use mobile sites, which build a server room in a shipping container or vehicle that can be easily transported to wherever it is needed.

Balanced site is not a standard term CISSP candidates need to know. 

Passive site is a reference to "active-passive" configurations that fail over to a standby that is not running like production. However, passive site is not a common term for describing a recovery site.

Mobile device management (MDM) is a software solution that helps with the challenging task of managing a myriad of mobile devices that employees use to access company resources. The goals of MDM are to protect the organization's data, provide monitoring, enable remote management, and support troubleshooting.

Application allow listing (historically referred to as whitelisting but sometimes considered racially insensitive) is a feature of MDM software. It is a list of software that the user is allowed to add to their mobile device if needed.

Encryption requirements are essential with mobile devices today (and just about any other device). This is included in the MDM software.

A hardware security module (HSM) is a type of tamper-resistant module used for cryptographic keys. An HSM would not be particularly useful in this case as employees are bringing their own devices that need to be remotely managed.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP)

Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is a communication protocol used to discover the link-layer address associated with a given Internet Protocol Version 4 (IPv4) address and is a critical function in the internet protocol suite.

Reverse Address Resolution Protocol (RARP) works in the opposite direction of ARP. It allows a device to obtain its IP address when it joins a network. The network administrators must manually program a link between a device's MAC address and an assigned IP address. This protocol is not commonly used.

Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) is the protocol of choice to dynamically assign IP addresses to devices when they join a network. It is used to configure network devices with information and resources such as an IP address, DNS server information, and NTP server information.

Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is used by network administrators. It allows visibility into the devices as well as configuration options.

A corrective control is a control that takes a non-working situation and brings it back to a functional state. For example, if there was a fire in the data center and the company failed to a hot site, they have used a corrective control. A recovery control returns things to a normal status. So if the company returns home they have recovered.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Diameter

Diameter was developed after and inspired by RADIUS to overcome the limitations associated with compatibility among other authentication mechanisms. Additionally, Diameter is able to separate authentication, authorization, and accounting services.

Terminal Access Controller Access-Control Service Plus (TACACS+) was not directly inspired by RADIUS, as TACACS+ was a Cisco development and RADIUS was developed by Livingston Enterprise. TACACS+ is an improvement to TACACS.

Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) is a protocol originally designed for the Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP) to allow one or two factors of authentication to be passed across an interface. It is commonly used today in other protocols like RADIUS. Transport Layer Service (TLS) is an improvement to the Secure Socket Layer (SSL), both of which are used in web-based connections for encryption purposes.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Privilege creep

Privilege creep happens when a user’s permissions are not revoked during role changes. This gives employees permission to access systems and resources they no longer need to do their job, which violates the principle of least privilege.

This was not a security breach. The employee did not knowingly or unknowingly access data they were not supposed to have access to, nor did they release or steal the data. 

East-west traversal describes the movement of an entity within a network. It is often used to describe how a threat actor may spread after breaching a network perimeter.

M of N control means that of the total number of things (N), a certain number (M) of them must be present. For example, 10 people may be participants in controlling access to video recordings, but six of those 10 must be present before the recording can be accessed.

result.prompt: A penetration tester has been hired by a large manufacturing organization and is testing to see if they can find hash collisions for passwords in a database they were able to capture. Of the following, what type of attack is the penetration tester MOST likely to use?

subtopics.name: 3.1 Research, implement and manage engineering processes using secure design principles
3.2 Understand the fundamental concepts of security models (e.g., Biba, Star Model, Bell-LaPadula)
3.3 Select controls based upon systems security requirements
3.4 Understand security capabilities of Information Systems (IS) (e.g., memory protection, Trusted Platform Module (TPM), encryption/decryption)
3.5 Assess and mitigate the vulnerabilities of security architectures, designs, and solution elements
3.6 Select and determine cryptographic solutions
3.7 Understand methods of cryptanalytic attacks
3.8 Apply security principles to site and facility design
3.9 Design site and facility security controls
3.10 Manage the information system lifecycle

result.explanation:
Correct answer: A birthday attack

A birthday attack exploits a mathematical principle on probability. This is known as the mathematical birthday paradox. For example, consider the scenario where a teacher with 30 students asks for everybody's birthday. The odds are small if the teacher picked a specific day (say, 5th of October) that at least one student was born on that particular day—around 8%. However, the probability that at least one student has the same birthday as any other student is about 70%. This same paradox can be used to find two passwords that produce the same hash value. This is known as a hash collision.

When discussing passwords, a brute force attack is usually interpreted as trying one password option after the next at the user interface attempting to login. 

A rainbow table is a table of hashes created for possible passwords. If a hash is captured, it can then be searched for in the rainbow table. When that hash is found it gives the attacker, or in this case a penetration tester, the password that generated that hash. The question is discussing hash collisions. That is two different passwords hashing to the same value. If there is a hash collision, it is possible that the rainbow table might reveal something that is not the actual password but hashes to the right value. That is not what the penetration tester is doing in the question.

A teardrop attack is not related to passwords or hashes. A teardrop attack is a type of Denial-of-Service (DoS) attack that exploits vulnerabilities in the IP fragmentation process of older versions of the Internet Protocol (IP).

Communication to stakeholders and regulators typically begins in the reporting phase of incident response. 

These are the phases in the incident response process, from earliest to latest:

  • Detection: Identify the intrusion using an IDS, anti-malware, or other means.
  • Response: Transfer control to the incident response team (IRT), who is responsible for investigating, mitigating, and recovering from the incident.
  • Reporting: Report information about the incident to internal stakeholders, regulators, customers, or law enforcement.
  • Recovery: Restore affected systems to a normal state via a reboot, restoration from backups, or complete rebuild.
  • Remediation: Perform root cause analysis (RCA) to identify and address the vulnerability that allowed the incident to occur.
  • Lessons learned: Perform a retrospective to identify potential inefficiencies or errors in the organization's response that could be corrected for future incidents.

Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service (RADIUS) centralizes authentication for remote connections. RADIUS has three components: the client or user, the RADIUS client, and the RADIUS server. The client/user will send their credentials to the RADIUS client and the RADIUS client will forward those credentials to the RADIUS server and wait for a reply. The RADIUS server will reply with the authorization of the client/user then the RADIUS client will grant or deny access based on the response from the RADIUS server.

RADIUS is generally used by network equipment to grant or deny access to network resources and it is frequently found in applications like 802.1X. RADIUS also provides accounting for each request, so all requests are tracked.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) with Encapsulating Security Protocol (ESP)

Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) is a suite of protocols that provide protection at the network layer of the Open System Interconnection (OSI) model. IPsec is frequently used to establish a Virtual Private Network (VPN) between two routers. IPsec protects the original Internet Protocol (IP) packet by encrypting or hashing the IP packet and adding a new Authentication Header (AH) or Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) header with a new IP header.

IPsec can be used in either AH or ESP mode:

  • Authentication Header (AH) provides integrity of the packet and adds an AH header. This includes authentication for each packet but no encryption.
  • Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) provides the confidentiality of the packet and adds an ESP header. This provides limited authentication for each packet and encryption of the original packet.

Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol (PPTP) is used when a Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP) connection needs to be extended through an IP network. Transport Layer Security (TLS) VPNs protect layers 5-7 of the OSI model and are typically not used for a gateway-to-gateway tunnel. TLS VPNs are usually used for remote users to connect to the corporate network.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Shared key

The Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) protocol defined in IEEE 802.11 uses a shared key between clients and access points. The access point sends the client a random value and the client encrypts this value using its shared key and sends it back to the access point. The access point decrypts the value with the shared key, and if the decrypted value is equal to the original, the access point authenticates the client. WEP is no longer considered secure and has many security flaws.

The shared key may appear to be a password that the user must type in, but it is actually the key. Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) and Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum (DSSS) are both methods of modulating wireless signals.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Single loss expectancy

The Single Loss Expectancy (SLE) is the monetary loss that an organization can expect if a specific threat is realized for a particular asset. The formula is SLE = AV (Asset Value) x EF (Exposure Factor). The AV is the full monetary value of the asset. The EF is the percentage of expected loss if a threat is realized.

As an example, if a building is worth $100,000, the AV = $100,000. If the EF for a fire is 50%, the EF = (.50). Using these values, the SLE would equal $50,000.

$100,000 x .50 = $50,000.

The Annualized Rate of Occurrence (ARO) is the estimate of how many times this will happen in a year. For example, if a fire is likely to happen once every two years, the ARO would be 1/2.

The Annualized Loss Expectancy (ALE) is the spreading of the SLE over the years of the ARO, or multiplied by the number of times in a year.  ALE = SLE x ARO.

So, for the fire, the ALE would be $50,000 x 1/2, which would be $25,000.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Confidentiality, integrity, availability

Confidentiality, integrity, and availability are at the heart of information security. Confidentiality ensures sensitive data is kept confidential and inaccessible by unauthorized individuals. Integrity keeps data authentic and unaltered. Availability ensures reliability and access to system resources. The following are common examples of technologies used to achieve these three different objectives:

  • Confidentiality: Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) encrypts data in transit to prevent eavesdropping.
  • Integrity: Secure Hash Algorithm (SHA-3) can be used to hash data and ensure it is unmodified when compared to a known good copy.
  • Availability: Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) helps ensure data remains available in the event of corruption of a specific partition or disk (Note: not all versions of RAID work if a full disk fails).

Hashing algorithms and techniques are commonly used to achieve nonrepudiation.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Bits

When a block cipher is used for encryption and decryption, a message is divided into blocks of bits. A block cipher first separates the message into chunks of bits and then applies the algorithm to the entire message. A Binary digIT (bit) is the basic unit of information in computing and can have only one of two values, 0 or 1.

Bits are grouped together in bytes. A byte is comprised, most commonly, of 8 bits. It is used to represent a single letter. Baud was a unit of speed seen in the days of the dial-up modems. Braid is a term seen around cabling, such as the Category 6 or 7 network wire cables.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Filtered

A filtered port is a port that the Nmap network scanner detects as being protected by a firewall. 

These are the most common Nmap port statuses:

  • Open: A port is open on a system and responds to a probe/connection request.
  • Closed: No application is accepting requests on the port.
  • Filtered: A firewall is interfering with an attempt to connect.
  • Unfiltered: Nmap cannot determine whether the port is open or closed.
  • Open|Filtered: Nmap cannot determine whether the port is open or filtered. This can occur if a port is opened but intentionally does not respond to Nmap probes.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Try...catch

Try...catch is a type of error handling logic that lets a developer define exactly how a program responds when an error is encountered. This can help improve the robustness of their code, but it must be implemented with care as logging logic that is too verbose could leak sensitive information. 

Compensating controls is a more high-level concept that includes any control implemented to address some of the risk associated with a security vulnerability. 

Code obfuscation is the process of making plaintext code difficult to read by obfuscating it. It does not directly address how errors or exceptions are handled. 

Input sanitization prevents untrusted inputs from leading to an injection attack in which user input causes unexpected or malicious results.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Maximize shareholder value

COBIT (formerly Control Objectives for Information and related Technology) is a framework for governance developed by the Information Systems Audit and Control Association (ISACA). The six COBIT 2019 governance system principles are:

  1. Provide stakeholder value: Ensure that governance delivers value by balancing benefits, risks, and resources. This is different from maximizing shareholder value, which can be applicable to publicly traded organizations. 
  2. Apply a holistic approach: Address governance through integrated components, including processes, structures, and information.
  3. Create a dynamic governance system: Adapt governance practices to changing environments and business needs.
  4. Separate governance from management: Distinguish strategic direction from operational execution.
  5. Tailor governance to enterprise needs: Customize governance based on organizational goals, size, and context.
  6. Ensure end-to-end governance: Extend governance across the entire organization, not just IT.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Risk

Risk is commonly defined with two keywords: likelihood or probability and impact or consequence. In the question, there is the possibility to represent the likelihood and the damage to represent the consequence. Risk management is used to reduce risk. Before any security policies are made, risk must always be defined and assessed within the organization.

When assessing risk, the following terms need to be identified and understood when talking about a specific asset:

A threat is defined by the United States National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) as any circumstance or event that can negatively impact a corporation's mission, operations, function, mission, etc.

A vulnerability is a weakness within the systems or procedures that can be exploited by the threat actor to cause damage.

Exposure is defined by NIST as the extent to which an organization is subject to risk.

result.prompt:
Sam, a network engineer for a mid-sized manufacturing organization, stumbled on sensitive documents between his boss and HR. The documents said the organization would terminate Sam’s employment at the end of the quarter due to the recent economic downturn. This disgruntled Sam, so he decided to configure critical systems to progressively fail and crash once his single sign-on (SSO) account was disabled. 

A few days after he was terminated, all core routers dropped their routing tables and crashed the entire network, resulting in massive financial losses.

Which term BEST describes this type of attack?

result.explanation:
Correct answer: A logic bomb

Logic bombs are programs or code that execute when certain conditions are met. It is common for IT or development personnel to hide malicious programs somewhere in a computer network that executes if their user account is ever disabled.

A buffer overflow occurs when a program tries to store more data in a buffer (temporary storage area) than it can hold. It can lead to data corruption, crashes, or even security vulnerabilities if exploited maliciously. However, the question does not indicate this occurred.

A backdoor is used for unauthorized access by an attacker. That is not what happened here. 

A time bomb is a type of malware that triggers at a specific date and/or time. There was no date or time-based trigger in this case.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Mandatory Access Control (MAC)

A system that employs Mandatory Access Control (MAC) uses classifications and labels to define user access. Every resource is classified with a label and users cannot access resources unless they have an equal or greater clearance level. MAC is widely used in government and military environments. MAC is often referred to as a lattice-based model because it looks like a garden lattice with well-defined boundaries when it is represented on paper.

Discretionary Access Control (DAC) allows the data owner to control and define access to objects. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) maps a subject’s role with their needed operations and tasks. Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) makes decisions based on attributes of the subject, object, or actions; such as time of day or object location.

result.prompt:
An organization just experienced a minor security breach in which a workstation was infected with malware. After reviewing Security Information and Event Manager (SIEM) logs, it was determined this malware did not spread or call out to a command and control (C2) server. Management later revealed it was due to a simulation training exercise in which an employee clicked a simulated malicious link in an email.

In what stage of the incident management process would management determine how to better prepare the workplace for the next potential incident?

subtopics.name: 6.1 Design and validate assessment, test, and audit strategies
6.2 Conduct security control testing
6.3 Collect security process data (e.g., technical and administrative)
6.4 Analyze test output and generate report
6.5 Conduct or facilitate security audits

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Lessons learned

This simulation exercise would allow management to recognize, during the lessons learned phase, how to reduce their risk of such an attack in the future. In this phase, all involved parties can reflect on what occurred from beginning to end. With this knowledge after a test, they can be better prepared for the future.

The reporting phase, when management and stakeholders are informed, typically occurs during the incident—well before the lessons learned phase.

Remediation is the step of actually fixing whatever issues led to the exploit to ensure they don't occur again. It occurs after management has already determined how to better prepare for another similar attack.

While the lessons learned may lead to new preventive measures, prevention occurs before an attack, while the question is about what should be done after an attack to prevent recurrence.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Serverless

Serverless architectures allow applications to run in an environment totally managed by the service provider. This relieves the developer of the responsibility of managing compute, storage, networking, etc.

Microservices break an application into different functional parts, which communicate via Application Programming Interfaces (APIs). These tend to be easier to deploy and scale than traditional applications but are harder to monitor.

Containerization places an application within a sandboxed environment containing all its dependencies. This enables containerized applications to be deployed anywhere regardless of the underlying infrastructure.

Embedded systems build specialized applications into single-purpose hardware. Often, embedded systems are used to interact with the physical world.

A simulation test is when the disaster recovery team is presented with a disaster scenario and is asked to come up with a response and then that response is tested. 

A parallel test is when the disaster recovery team relocates personnel to the recovery site and implements site activation procedures.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Initialization Vector (IV)

An Initialization Vector (IV) is a random value used with a key to encrypt or decrypt data. The IV is used to reduce the likelihood of the same plaintext patterns from being found in the ciphertext. The IV is used to randomize the plaintext before it is encrypted with the symmetric key. Increasing the size of the encryption key makes it harder to brute force the key and decrypt data, but it has no impact on altering patterns.

When a symmetric block algorithm is used, it can be placed in one of a number of different modes. The Electronic Code Book (ECB) mode is the only one that does not use an IV or something similar. So, all patterns that are in the plaintext would exist and be discoverable in the ciphertext.

Stream ciphers do not use an IV, they function in a different manner from the block algorithms. These are very difficult to create and also difficult to implement in software properly. Therefore, in general, they are not the solution to the patterns in the plaintext.

One of the reasons Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) was weak was that it used a short 24-bit IV. This caused the same IV to be used multiple times throughout the stream, allowing attackers to find patterns between messages using the same IV.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Edge

Data loss prevention (DLP) solutions can be network, endpoint, or cloud solutions — not edge. They attempt to block sensitive data from being exfiltrated from an organization’s systems. They can use data labels or look for patterns associated with certain types of sensitive data. DLP systems come in three types:

  • Network: Network DLP solutions inspect the content of network traffic, looking for signs of attempted data exfiltration and preventing it from leaving the network.
  • Endpoint: Endpoint DLP solutions can be used to manage sensitive data stored on a system or sent to external devices. For example, an endpoint DLP solution could prevent printing sensitive data or saving it to a USB drive.
  • Cloud DLP: Cloud DLP solutions are network DLP solutions designed to operate in cloud environments.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: External

External audits are performed by an external organization. Often, they are paid for by the organization, which has a certain level of control over it. However, they are considered more trustworthy than an internal audit since the external auditor is independent of the company under test.

The other two audit types are as follows:

  • Internal: Internal audits are performed by the organization’s own staff and for its purposes. For example, they may be intended to prove that the company is meeting its security goals.
  • Third Party: Third-party audits are controlled and conducted by third parties. A regulator may select or accredit the auditor and can use the results to determine compliance.

In degaussing, a magnetic field is created that realigns the magnetic fields on media. It's one way to remove data remanence on media such as a hard drive or tape drive. It is effective only on magnetic media, so it can't be used on media such as DVD or CD discs.

Degaussing is not used for decryption or encryption.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Entitlement

Entitlement refers to the level of privileges granted to a user. If a user has been granted access to an object, they are entitled to it.

The other three options are not used to describe the level of privileges that are granted. Scope of role comes close if the access control system is a Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) system, but it is not usually stated that way. Aggregation is the idea of adding various things together and can be used in many different situations. It is a problem when dealing with databases. The concern is that a user may be able to aggregate different pieces of information together that disclose a piece of information that has a higher level of classification than they should be able to see. Seniority is a status in business, but not in access control.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Full interruption

A full-interruption test switches operations from the primary site to the recovery site. 

Testing disaster response plans is essential to ensure they are effective and nothing is missed. Testing can be performed in various ways:

  • Full-interruption test: A full-interruption test switches operations from the primary site to the recovery site. This is more disruptive and risky than a parallel test but verifies that the organization’s failover processes work.
  • Walkthrough: In a walkthrough, the team physically performs the actions described in the plan (unless it would disrupt operations). This can build familiarity and help identify parts of the plan that are impossible or require additional resources.
  • Simulation: In a simulation, like a fire drill, the team is given a scenario and tasked with responding to it. This is more realistic than a walkthrough but can be more disruptive to operations since tasks are actually completed.
  • Parallel test: Parallel tests perform normal business operations at an alternate site as well as the primary site. This ensures the alternate site can complete its duties while minimizing the impact on normal operations.
  • Read-through/tabletop: A read-through or tabletop exercise involves reading through and roleplaying the disaster response plan. This is the cheapest, least disruptive, and least realistic form of testing.

Red Team and Blue Team are offensive and defensive security teams, respectively, in an organization. They are not types of diaster recovery tests.

Preventive controls are used to thwart or stop unwanted or unauthorized activity from occurring. They are designed to keep errors or irregularities from happening. Fences, locks, and mantraps are all examples of physical preventive access controls, or deterrent controls.

Detective controls, such as logs and video recordings, tell the organization that something happened. They do not stop or prevent anything from happening.

Corrective controls return something from a non-working state to a working state. A recovery control returns things to a normal working state. One example of a corrective control is a disaster recovery site, where the recovery control is rebuilding and returning to the home location.

An administrative control is neither technical nor physical. Policies and procedures are good examples of administrative controls.

A Business Continuity Plan (BCP) is a series of procedures and plans that help an organization maintain operations in a long-term disaster. They are often confused with Disaster Recovery Plans (DRP) but differ in their scope. A BCP is generally focused on the business as a whole, whereas a DRP is generally focused on critical IT infrastructure and processes. A BCP and DRP are used together to recover from and maintain operations during a disaster.

Incident Response Plan (IRP) is incorrect because it focuses on an organization's response to a suspected security event. Crisis Communications Plan (CCP) is incorrect because it focuses on maintaining communications during a disaster.

result.prompt: What is an evil twin attack?

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
4.2 Secure network components
4.3 Implement secure communication channels according to design

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Manipulation of wireless clients to connect to a rogue access point by spoofing a legitimate service set identifier (SSID)

An evil twin attack works by manipulating a wireless client to connect to a malicious access point. Hackers do this by spoofing a legitimate service set identifier (SSID) and basic service set identifier (BSSID) that the wireless client already trusts. When a client connects to the malicious access point, the hacker can see all network traffic between the client and web servers. This is a type of man-in-the-middle (MITM) attack.

An unauthorized access point that has been added to the company network by a user or attacker is called a rogue access point.

Deauthentication frames are defined in the IEEE 802.11 standard and are used to terminate a wireless connection. Flooding the environment with such frames would cause a denial-of-service (DoS) attack.

Social engineering attacks aim to exploit human behavior and trick people. A highly targeted attack may be spear phishing or a similar personalized attack, but it is not an evil twin attack.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: DAST

Organizations can use various forms of testing to identify flaws in application code, including:

  • Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST): DAST analyzes a running application for vulnerabilities by providing it with inputs and monitoring their results. Fuzzing is a type of DAST.
  • Static Application Security Testing (SAST): SAST often inspects the source code of the application to identify common flaws in the code. It can be applied early in the SDLC because it doesn’t require a completed, runnable application.
  • Interactive Application Security Testing (IAST): IAST combines internal visibility into an application with dynamic testing to enhance vulnerability detection.
  • Software Composition Analysis (SCA): SCA identifies vulnerabilities inherited from third-party libraries and dependencies, protecting against supply chain vulnerabilities.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Internet Protocol Security

Internet protocol security (IPsec) is a suite of protocols that provides protection at the network layer of the Open System Interconnection (OSI) model. IPsec is frequently used to establish a Virtual Private Network (VPN) between two routers. IPsec protects the original IP packet by encrypting or hashing the IP packet and adding a new AH or ESP header with a new IP header. IPsec-specific protocols are:

  • Authentication Header (AH) provides integrity of the packet and adds an AH header.
  • Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) provides the confidentiality of the packet and adds an ESP header.
  • Internet Key Exchange (IKE) is used to negotiate tunnel parameters.

Transport Layer Security (TLS) is used to encrypt data in transmission, most commonly in web-based sessions. There is authentication at the beginning of the setup of the encrypted connection. It can even be mutual authentication. However, it is not an option in the question. The question says OR. In IPSec you can choose just Authentication Header (AH) and not enable ESP. The same is true with Secure Shell (SSH). SSH is used to encrypt the data transmission. Encryption is not an option, it is the purpose.

Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) is a protocol from Microsoft that allows for an encrypted remote connection. It has the purpose of a remote connection. It encrypts traffic, and there are many options within. However, it is not designed for authentication.

5.3 Federated identity with a third-party service

result.explanation:
Correct answer: RADIUS sends usernames in cleartext from the RADIUS client to the server.

Sending usernames in cleartext can be problematic, as someone sniffing network traffic can see the username and guess a password associated with that username. RADIUS will only hash the passwords transmitted between the server and its client, using a single-challenge response for authentication, authorization, and accountability purposes. To combat the issue of plaintext usernames, organizations can implement Transport Layers Service (TLS) to encrypt all information.

RADIUS is not a new protocol as it was invented at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) during the Athena project in the early 1990s. RADIUS does not use a challenge-response to authenticate the user, but that is not a major flaw. RADIUS does hash passwords.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Microsegmentation

Microsegmentation divides the network into tiny segments (as small as a single device) to achieve extremely granular control over network traffic. Microsegmentation is essential for a zero-trust security model.

Logical segmentation uses VLANs, VPNs, and other devices to logically divide traffic into isolated networks that are on the same physical network.

Physical segmentation uses physically separated network components. The three types include:

  • Air-gapped: Two networks are physically disconnected from one another, providing the strongest level of segmentation.
  • In-band: This sends both data and control traffic over the same network segment but doesn't actually use physical segmentation.
  • Out-of-band: Data and control traffic are separated onto different paths, and some traffic may have its own, isolated path.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Kerberos exploitation attack

Kerberos is a widely adopted authentication protocol that relies on a mechanism of ticket-granting ticket (TGT) and ticket-granting service (TGS) tickets. Kerberos exploitation attacks are a category of cryptanalytic attacks that exploit weaknesses in this mechanism. Specific attacks in this category include golden ticket, silver ticket, pass the ticket, overpass the hash, and kerberoasting.

Statistical attacks attempt to exploit weaknesses in the underlying hardware or application delivering cryptography (e.g., simulated random number generation vs. true random number generation).

Birthday attacks are attacks that aim to exploit the popular "birthday paradox" to identify hash collisions and use them to compromise a system or data (e.g., by finding a matching password hash). Birthday attacks are not specifically focused on Kerberos.

TGT cracking is not a standard attack type.

result.prompt: Which wireless access protocol FIRST introduced forward secrecy (FS)?

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
4.2 Secure network components
4.3 Implement secure communication channels according to design

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Wi-Fi Protected Access 3 (WPA3)

Forward secrecy (FS), sometimes referred to as perfect forward secrecy (PFS), is used to prevent the compromise of a long-term secret key from affecting the confidentiality of past transmissions. For example, suppose an attacker compromised a private key used by an asymmetric algorithm to exchange a symmetric encryption key. In that case, the attacker could decrypt all transmissions they have recorded.

WPA3 replaces pre-shared keys (PSK) with Simultaneous Authentication of Equals (SAE). SAE uses zero-knowledge proof instead of sending a hash of the password to the access point. WPA3 uses the Dragonfly Key Exchange, similar to Diffie–Hellman, to exchange keys and provides FS. Like WPA2, WPA3 still uses AES-CCMP to encrypt all wireless transmissions. SAE is not a wireless access protocol per se; it is used by WPA3. 

WEP was designed to provide confidentiality and privacy for wireless communications by encrypting data transmitted over a Wi-Fi network. It relies on static keys, which are not regularly changed, making it vulnerable to key compromise and unauthorized access. WEP's reuse of IVs can lead to predictable encryption patterns and facilitate attacks, such as the IV collision attack.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Vulnerability assessments

Security testing comes in a variety of different forms:

  • Vulnerability assessments: Vulnerability assessments use automated tools to identify vulnerabilities in an organization’s systems, including networks, web applications, and databases. Typically they check an application against the list of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) to identify known issues. These vulnerabilities are scored using the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS), which helps identify how severe the vulnerability is.
  • Penetration testing: Pen testing includes vulnerability assessments but also attempts to exploit the vulnerabilities they discover. Additionally, it involves more manual testing than a fully automated vulnerability scan.
  • Breach and attack simulation (BAS): BAS platforms are designed to perform automated penetration testing. They introduce indicators of compromise (IoCs) into the system—malicious files, C2 traffic, etc.—and check whether the corporate security controls identify them. 
  • Compliance checks: Compliance checks verify that an organization implements the security controls required by applicable regulations and that these controls are functional.

IoC testing is a distractor answer and not a standard term.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Anonymization

Anonymization is the process of removing data to the point that it is impossible to identify the subject(s). This is most effective with large data sets with many categories. Anonymization also cannot be reversed, making it impossible to use a secondary data set to retrace steps associated with the anonymization process. What sets it apart is anonymization can't be reversed because the technique requires the shuffling of a large data set and has no database to link the random data back to the original subject(s).

Pseudonymization does not remove any data and instead provides false names for subjects. While it may seem like an effective method to protect data, those with knowledge of the fact that the data is using pseudonyms can narrow down the actual identities of subjects based on the categories of traits. Tokenization involves replacing sensitive data with a token that has no actual relation to the data it is replacing. With both pseudonymization and tokenization, a separate grouping of data linking the two together is kept and can be linked back together by those who made the data. Limitation is a fabricated term.

M of N control requires that a minimum number of authorized users (M) be present out of all authorized users (N) before performing a function. For example, a dual custody safe may have three keys and require that two of the three keys be present before opening. M of N control is a form of split knowledge. Split knowledge separates a piece of information, say a password or combination for a safe, between multiple people.

In split knowledge, everyone needs to show up to be able to use the information. The question says ‘requiring a minimum number’. That changes the answer to M of N. Separation of duties takes all of the steps within a task and then divides it between at least two people. All of the people do not have to be present to complete the task. The first person could complete their steps one day and then the second person on the next day. Software escrow involves having the source code for software developed by a contracted company be placed into safe storage. Evidence collected as part of a digital forensics process should meet these requirements:

result.prompt:
Roberta is a hacktivist who has discovered a group of government servers that are vulnerable to an attack that allows her to flood the server's broadcast address with Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) requests containing a victim's Internet Protocol (IP) address as the source address.

Of the following, what type of attack has Roberta MOST likely discovered is possible?

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
4.2 Secure network components
4.3 Implement secure communication channels according to design

result.explanation:
Correct answer: A smurf attack

A smurf attack spoofs the source IP address with the victim's address and floods the broadcast address with Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) requests. This causes devices on the network to send an ICMP reply to the victim for each ICMP request sent by the attacker. This overwhelms the victim and can cause the system to crash. A smurf attack is a Denial of Service attack (DoS).

In a SYN flood attack, the attacker floods the target server with a large number of SYN packets, typically spoofing the source IP addresses to make it appear as though the requests are coming from legitimate clients. However, the attacker does not complete the handshake process by sending the final ACK packet to establish the connection. As a result, the target server is left waiting for the final ACK packet, tying up system resources and preventing it from processing legitimate connection requests.

A buffer overflow attack is a type of security vulnerability that occurs when a program attempts to write more data to a buffer, or temporary storage area, than it can hold. Buffers are allocated a fixed amount of memory, and if a program writes data beyond the allocated buffer size, it can overwrite adjacent memory locations. This overflow can corrupt data, crash the program, or, more dangerously, allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code.

In a land attack, the attacker sends a spoofed TCP SYN packet with the source IP address set to the same IP address as the target system as well as the same port number for both the source and destination ports. This creates a situation where the target system receives a packet that appears to come from itself. When the target system attempts to process the packet, it enters into an infinite loop of responding to itself, causing it to become overwhelmed and unable to process legitimate network traffic.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Deterrent control

Deterrent controls attempt to discourage someone from taking a specific action. A high fence with lights at night is a physical deterrent control. A strict security policy stating severe consequences for employees if it is violated is an example of an administrative deterrent control. A proxy server that redirects a user to a warning page when a user attempts to access a restricted site is an example of a technical deterrent control.

Preventive controls attempt to prevent incidents before they occur. A firewall is a technical preventive control because it can prevent malicious traffic from entering a network. A guard is a physical preventive control. Administrative preventive controls include access reviews and audits.

Corrective controls attempt to modify the environment after an incident. It does not return the environment to normal, but it does arrest the bad situation such as the spread of a virus. Antivirus software that quarantines a virus is an example of a technical corrective control. A fire extinguisher is an example of a physical corrective control.

Recovery controls provide methods to recover from an incident. Recovery returns the environment back to a normal condition.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Secure defaults

The potential risks introduced by unconfigured settings are best addressed through the secure design principle of secure defaults. This principle demands product and solution teams consider the security implications of weak "default" settings in their product or solution (e.g. passwords, algorithms, or controls) and instead utilize responsible default security settings, even if those increase the complexity of implementation or use.

Trust but verify is a secure design principle that challenges assumptions of trust derived from certain criteria without trust being explicitly verified (e.g. traffic originating from an internal network). Separation of duties is a secure design principle that demands a sensitive task be split between two or more individuals to reduce the risk of fraud, abuse, or errors. Fail securely is a secure design principle that bids developers consider the security implications of exceptions (errors) in their code and incorporate error handling routines that manage them, to preserve the security of the application (and the data accessible through it).

result.explanation:
Correct answer: It's prohibitive

The Mandatory Access Control (MAC) model is prohibitive by design, as it employs an implicit-deny methodology. MAC uses classifications and labels to define user access. Every resource is classified with a label, and users cannot access resources unless they have an equal or greater clearance level. MAC is widely used in government and military environments.

Attribute-based would be called Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC). ABAC allows for the configuration of controls based on a variety of different assets. Those could be where the user is (home, office, etc.), what kind of network the user is connecting from (wired, wireless, cellular, etc.), and so on. Role-based would be called Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). RBAC controls access based on the role the user is assigned and then what permissions that role is granted. None of the models would be considered permissive.

Risk is viewed as the possibility that something could happen to damage, destroy, or disclose data or other resources with a discussion of the consequence to the organization. Risk assessment and management are used to reduce risk to an acceptable level.

A vulnerability is a weakness or flaw in a system. When a threat agent exploits a vulnerability, it can cause loss. Vulnerabilities could be flaws in a system or flaws in a process.

An attack occurs when a threat agent attempts to exploit a vulnerability in a system to bring about a threat..

Correct answer: Follows a program as it runs to ensure each function and to spot and prevent unusual behavior

Runtime Application Self-Protection (RASP) is a security application that ensures all software runs as it should and does not execute behavior that may be malicious. RASP digs into the code associated with the program, views what is set to occur at runtime, and determines if it's malicious.

RASP doesn't necessarily prevent a program from crashing at boot, conduct a static analysis, or enhance the efficiency of a program. In fact, RASP is known to slow programs down and sometimes hinder performance. The protection it offers occurs during a dynamic analysis, not static.

Network discovery scanners are used to explore a network and are most commonly used in penetration tests. One type of network discovery scanner is a port scanner, which looks for open Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP) ports on a network.

The Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) Top Ten list is a list of the ten most popular web application risks. Among the list are insufficient logging, security misconfiguration, and using components with known vulnerabilities. These are risks associated with any business, so educating employees properly will ensure these issues (and many more not on the list) are significantly reduced.

The MITRE ATT&CK Framework is a detailed explanation of techniques used by attackers, which can sometimes be used by penetration testers to replicate attacks. Although it would be helpful to the company, it would be comprised of plenty of unnecessary information not tailored to the business's needs. result.explanation:
Correct answer: A worm

A worm is a type of malware that can reproduce without a legitimate host application. Worms spread on their own. They crawl into a computer, cause damage, and then head back out on the network to the next computer it can find to infect. Viruses cannot reproduce without a legitimate host application. Viruses infect legitimate files or programs and use them to spread themselves. Generally a virus requires a human to take some action that will begin the process of infection and reproduction. For example, opening an infected file, infected email attachment, hover over an infected picture and so on.

A virus is a type of malicious software that infects computer systems by replicating itself and spreading to other files or devices. It can damage data, disrupt system operations, steal information, and sometimes even render the infected system unusable, posing significant cybersecurity threats. Most viruses require user interaction to initiate the infection and replication.

A rootkit is a type of malicious software that allows unauthorized access and control over a computer or network. It is designed to conceal its presence and provide stealthy access to system resources, enabling attackers to perform malicious activities undetected.

A trojan, short for trojan horse, is a type of malicious software disguised as a legitimate program or file. Once installed, it performs unauthorized actions such as stealing data, damaging files, or granting remote access to attackers without the user's knowledge.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Perform backups

A custodian is defined as someone entrusted with guarding and protecting something. Data custodians are responsible for maintaining the data and ensuring its availability for the data owner. A data custodian could be considered anyone who is in possession of a data asset. It certainly includes the Information Technology (IT) department. The data custodians are responsible for backing up data to ensure its security.

The data custodian does not determine access permissions. That should be determined by the data owner who knows and specifies who has a need to know. It is possible that the data custodian would be given instructions to delete data, but that is not the most likely action they would take. It is not a requirement to consider data custodians as those in the IT department. result.explanation:
Correct answer: RAID-0

Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) is used to group disks and provide fault tolerance or increase performance. In this scenario, you should choose RAID-0 to increase the write speed of each node. Since the cluster of servers replicates data itself, it is not necessary for the RAID array to duplicate data or add parity, which makes RAID-0 ever more acceptable.

The levels of RAID are as follows:

  • RAID-0 strips data across multiple disks. This increases the chance of failure but increases the write and read speed.
  • RAID-1 mirrors data across multiple disks. This decreases the usable drive space by 50% and does not provide any write speed benefits, which are important in this case. 
  • RAID-5 strips data across multiple disks and adds a parity bit. This provides fault tolerance but decreases write speed, which is important in this case. 
  • RAID-6 adds a second parity block to the standard RAID-5 approach. It can therefore be slower and less performant, which makes it a suboptimal choice in this case.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Authority

Social engineering aims to exploit human nature. These are some common principles of human nature that social engineers exploit:

  • Authority: Victims are more likely to obey if they think the attacker is someone with authority (e.g., an executive or law enforcement).
  • Intimidation: Scare tactics may compel a target to take action on behalf of a social engineer.
  • Consensus: Social proof or making a target feel as though "everyone is doing it" can help a social engineer convince their victims to perform a desired action.
  • Trust: Building a false sense of trust with the victim, such as a working relationship established over time, can lead a victim to do things they might not otherwise. 

The threat actor is acting as Acme Inc.'s executive, a position of authority, so authority is the best answer here.

Correct answer: Advanced persistent threat (APT)

An advanced persistent threat (APT) is usually carried out by a group of attackers who work together to target a specific organization. These attacks are often state-sponsored. When their skill sets are combined, the attackers are very skilled. APTs exercise patience to reduce the likelihood of discovery and increase the possibility of success.

A man-in-the-middle (MITM) attack occurs when some attacker inserts themselves into the middle of the communication stream between the client and server. The attacker could just be watching and gathering information, making them very difficult to detect. They may also alter the data and then forward it to cause some other problem.

A logic bomb is a type of malicious software that "explodes," or becomes active, at a specific time or under a specific condition. An example is the Michelangelo virus, which explodes every year on his birthday, although there may not be any systems on the planet that are still vulnerable.

The Biba model is designed to protect integrity. Its three principles are the following:

result.prompt: Which of the following is an example of a layer 2 network device used for network segmentation and traffic isolation?

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
4.2 Secure network components
4.3 Implement secure communication channels according to design

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Switch

A switch is generally considered to be a layer 2 device. However, Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) switches are layer 1 devices, and there are Internet Protocol (IP)-based layer 3 devices. So, a layer 2 switch refers to Ethernet switches. The job of an Ethernet switch is to create individual broadcast zones for each port on the switch. This is a form of network segmentation. The switch will isolate traffic based on the destination Media Access Control (MAC) address that the frame is being sent to.

Firewalls are designed to block or allow traffic to pass based on the configured rules (or policies). Firewalls operate at layer 3 if it uses the IP address to make decisions or layer 4 if it uses the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) or User Datagram Protocol (UDP) port to make decisions. Firewalls could also operate at layer 5 or layer 7. The firewall operates in a top-down manner, first matching the incoming packet to the top rule. If the packet or contained data matches the rule, the designated rule (block or allow) is followed. If it does not match the first rule, it is compared to the second rule and so on. The final rule should block all other traffic.

A router operates at layer 3. The router will route traffic out specific ports based on the IP destination address in the IP packet. Routers create segments based on the IP subnet assigned to each port.

Gateways are essentially firewalls, but they operate at layer 7 of the Open System Interconnect (OSI) model.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Hot site

A hot site provides the most rapid recovery capability because it includes the full resources required for instant function and connectivity of IT systems. A hot site is missing only people and some data.

A hot site can help ensure high availability (HA). However, HA site is not a standard term for a type of disaster recovery site. 

A warm site is basically a cold site, but with computers and communication links already in place, ready to be loaded with operating systems and data. 

In a reciprocal agreement, two organizations pledge the availability of their organization's data center in the event of a disaster, but it may take time to move to a reciprocal site and start working. This is not faster because the other company's site would not have any of the data, and the other company may need time to release access to some systems.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Measures risk consistently and objectively according to a set formula

Quantitative risk management deals with the exact quantities of factors involved in risk. It measures the anticipated loss numerically using the single loss expectancy (SLE), annual rate of occurrence (ARO), and annualized loss expectancy (ALE) formulas. Quantitative risk management assessments can use past data and information to help predict the future.

Qualitative risk management attempts to assign priorities of importance, distinguishing lower-risk factors from higher-risk factors. This allows scenarios to be created to portray which risk is the most serious and needs the most attention. Quantitative loss can be measured numerically, but qualitative loss is measured subjectively.

Quantitative risk assessments would not necessarily define the characteristics of a risk that are most relevant to an organization.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Database Activity Monitor

A Database Activity Monitor (DAM) is a security tool that continuously monitors and audits database activity to detect unauthorized access, data breaches, or suspicious activities. It provides real-time alerts, log analyses, and forensic capabilities to enhance database security and compliance.

A File Activity Monitor (FAM) is a security tool designed to track and monitor user interactions with files and data stored on a computer or network. It records file access, modification, deletion, and transfer activities to detect unauthorized or suspicious actions, prevent data leaks, and ensure compliance with security policies. File activity monitors provide real-time alerts, detailed logs, and reporting capabilities to enhance data security and protect sensitive information.

DAMs and FAMs are not in any of the listed references. Unfortunately, these books do not contain all of the topics you could encounter on the test. These two are the newest products listed here and they are in the Certified Cloud Security Professional (CCSP) exam, so it is possible to run into them here. They are most closely related to firewalls. They initially only monitored traffic, however, they are now starting to block traffic like a firewall does.

A firewall is a network security device or software that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined security rules. It acts as a barrier between trusted internal networks and untrusted external networks to prevent unauthorized access and potential cyber threats.

A Web Application Firewall (WAF) is a security solution designed to protect web applications from a wide range of cyber threats and attacks. It sits between the web application and the client (user) and acts as a filter to monitor, intercept, and block malicious traffic before it reaches the application server.
