result.explanation:
Correct answer: File Transfer Protocol Secure (FTPS) server

An FTPS server will allow for secure file transfers across the internet. However, it is not a program meant for the administration of a network.

Open LDAP, Kerberos, and FreeIPA are all programs built to meet the needs of central administration for many workstations. Open LDAP and FreeIPA are essentially open-source versions of Microsoft Active Directory. Each program allows for the administration of any workstation within the domain, granting or denying access to resources, and the administration of patching from one administrator workstation.

Kerberos is a network authentication protocol that verifies the identities of users and services in a secure manner. It uses encryption and a trusted third party (Key Distribution Center) to issue and manage authentication tokens, facilitating secure communication while minimizing exposure to password theft or eavesdropping.

Open Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) is an open-source implementation of the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP). It manages and provides directory services, like user authentication and directory lookups, making it vital for centralized user management in networks.

Free Identity, Policy, Audit (FreeIPA) is an open-source identity management system built on top of LDAP. It provides centralized authentication, authorization, and account information for Linux and Unix-like systems. It includes features like Single Sign-On (SSO) and policy enforcement.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: The work factor

When file encryption is strong, it is said to have increased the work factor level. Work factor refers to the difficulty of breaking an encrypted file. Therefore, it takes significantly more time to hack or break.

Substitution and transposition are two different types of encryption techniques. They are both used together in block ciphers today. Substitution is the method of altering plaintext by replacing a value with a different value. A simple example is the Caesar cipher. If you assign a number to each letter of the alphabet (a=1, b=2, c=3 and so on) and then add a value (such as 3) to a letter in the plaintext, (for example the first word in the question “when” where w=23) So w=23 + 3 = 26. The 26th letter of the alphabet is Z. So Z would be the ciphertext value.

Transposition is the process of altering the order of the plaintext in order to encrypt it. If the plaintext is again ‘when’ the ciphertext could be ‘hwne’. All of the letters are still there, they are just in a different order now. Today’s block cipher does a combination of both substitution and transposition.

Claude Shannon, at Belcore, wrote a paper in 1945 explaining that confusion and diffusion are two critical concepts in cryptography today. Diffusion speaks to the relationship between the plaintext and the ciphertext. Basically, what is wanted is to ensure that patterns in the plaintext do not appear in the ciphertext.

result.prompt: The TCP/IP model consists of how many layers?

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Four

The Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol (TCP/IP) model consists of four layers. The four layers are Application, Transport or Host-to-Host, Internet, and Network Access. They correspond to layers within the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model. Sometimes the TCP/IP model is shown as a five-layer model, as shown below. The TCP/IP was invented long ago, before the OSI model and therefore the names used for the layers are terms that we do not use today, so we have adopted a couple of different representations of the TCP/IP model.

The layers of the TCP/IP model are:

  • Application
  • Host-to-Host (or transport)
  • Internet (or Internetwork, Internetworking or Network)
  • Link (or combine this with physical and call it network access)
  • Physical

The seven layers of the OSI model are:

  • Application
  • Presentation
  • Session
  • Transport
  • Network
  • Data Link
  • Physical

Sometimes the physical and the link layers are considered one and called network access. The host-to-host layer equates to the transport layer of the OSI model and is sometimes called the transport layer. The top three layers of the OSI model are represented in the TCP/IP model as the application layer. There is often confusion in conversations due to this.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Detective

Detective controls are deployed to detect or identify unwanted or unauthorized activity. These controls are frequently deployed after an event to ensure that future occurrences are discovered. Detective controls do not directly block or prevent unwanted activity. Detective controls include security cameras, motion detectors, and virus scans.

Corrective and recovery controls are very similar to each other. A corrective control takes something from a non-functional state to a functional one. A Disaster Recovery (DR) site is a good example. If there has been a fire in the data center, the DR site allows the business to get back to a functioning state. It is not normal though, as they do not have all systems running and they are in different locations. If the data center is rebuilt after the fire and all systems are returned to a ‘normal’ state, then a recovery control has been used. Recovery controls take broken or only functional environments/systems back to a normal condition.

A deterrent control is something that, when it is known by the would-be attacker, they decide not to do their bad deed as they are deterred from that behavior. An armed guard deters someone from breaking into a building. Or a policy that when violated could cost someone their job is also a deterrent.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Preventive controls

Preventive controls are the best at reducing risk since they directly stop an unwanted action. Detective, corrective, deterrent, recovery, and compensating controls also reduce risk but work in a complementary manner with preventive controls that help create an organization's overall security posture. Preventive controls include gates, fences, anti-virus software, and smart cards.

Detective controls inform by recording or notifying the operations center that there are problems somewhere. Corrective controls return broken systems or services to a functional state. This state is likely not a normal state, but it does allow the business to continue. Recovery controls would return the system back to a normal state. Deterrent controls have the effect that the threat actor would be dissuaded from launching an attack.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Secure Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions

Secure Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) are used to encrypt and digitally sign emails. S/MIME uses the RSA encryption algorithm and has been incorporated into many commercial products, such as Microsoft Outlook, Mozilla Thunderbird, and MAC OS X Mail. S/MIME relies on the use of the X.509 certificates for exchanging cryptographic keys.

The Post Office Protocol (POP) 3 is a basic protocol that enables a user to access their emails. It works by downloading the messages off of the server onto the local device. That provides little security because the email is not on the central email server. However, the emails are sent in the clear and are not encrypted. There is no confidentiality. Anyone listening will see the text of your email.

Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is a protocol that enables the sending of emails. It transmits from the email client to the server. However, the emails are sent in the clear, just as they are with POP3.

Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) changes the older logic of POP and SMTP by leaving the emails on the server. This is what allows the same emails to show on a mobile phone, a desktop computer, and a tablet all at the same time. It too sends emails in the clear. It is possible to use Transport Layer Security (TLS) (formerly SSL) to encrypt the sent and received. Technically, that is IMAPS and the question only has IMAP as a possible answer.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Identification

In order for any security system to operate, it must first identify the subject. Systems must perform Identification, Authentication, Authorization, and Accountability. These are the four elements of IAAA service. Identification is when a user asserts their identity using their user ID, user name, email, or personal number.

Authentication is the step to prove that identity assertion or verification. Authentication is done using one or more of the factors of authentication. Factor 1 is something that you know, such as a password. Factor 2 is something that you have, such as a token, card, or authentication tool. Factor 3 is something that you are, which would be biometrics such as a fingerprint, retinal pattern, or vocal pattern. Authorization is then granting the user permissions (or not) now that their identification has been verified. Accountability is then tracking the user's activity by creating a log of their activities.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Corrective

These are the main types of security controls:

  • Corrective: Corrective controls fix issues after a security incident. Anti-malware that removes an infection and an auto-close arm on a door are examples of corrective controls.
  • Preventive: Preventive controls are designed to stop an incident from happening. Fences, locks, and access controls are examples of preventive controls.
  • Deterrent: Deterrent controls attempt to discourage an attacker. Corporate policies and security cameras are examples of deterrent controls.
  • Compensating: Compensating controls are used as a replacement when the preferred control is unusable. For example, a company renting an office in a building may put locks on the doors when it can't build a fence.
  • Detective: Detective controls help to identify that an incident is occurring. CCTV, audit trails, and honeypots are examples of detective controls.
  • Recovery: Recovery controls restore normal operations after an incident to a greater extent than corrective ones. Backups and server clusters are examples of recovery controls.

Restorative is not a standard type of security control.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Substitution cipher

In substitution ciphers, each letter is replaced by an alternative letter. For instance, each A is replaced with the letter G. ROT13 is an old, popular substitution cipher that substitutes each letter with the 13th letter from the current letter's position. For each A there is an N. For each B there is an O, etc.

Transposition ciphers alter the order of the letters of the plaintext. For example, encryption of the plaintext HELLO could become the ciphertext of LLEOH (depending on the cipher and key). But all the letters from the plaintext are still there, they are just in a different order. A one-time pad is a substitution cipher that uses a key that is as long as the plaintext and properly random and only used once. They are provably unbreakable by brute force attacks. A running key cipher is a substitution cipher that uses a key as long as the plaintext.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Secure real-time transport protocol (SRTP)

Real-Time Transport Protocol (RTP) carries the media packets for voice or video communications over an IP-based network. RTP settings are negotiated between endpoints by the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP). Media packets can be encrypted by using the Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP). When SRTP is used, the SIP protocol generally exchanges the symmetric encryption keys between the caller and callee. To protect the keys, Transport Layer Security (TLS) is used to encrypt the SIP headers. This is sometimes referred to as SIP Secure (SIPS).

SIP Secure (SIPS) is incorrect because SIPS is used for signaling. It does not carry the actual media between each endpoint; it is used to set up the phone call connection across the network.

Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) is incorrect because it is a category of technologies related to the transmission of voice and multimedia data over IP-based networks, not a specific protocol or mechanism for securing media.

Transport Layer Security (TLS) is incorrect because it protects SIP headers and key exchanges, not the RTP media packets.

result.prompt: Which of the following attacks BEST exploits a flaw in a system’s ability to reassemble oversized fragmented packets?

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
4.2 Secure network components

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Teardrop attack

A teardrop attack exploits a flaw in a system’s ability to reassemble oversized fragmented packets. Attackers intentionally send oversized fragmented packets with an offset and size that are incorrect, causing the victim system to crash when they are reassembled.

An Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) poisoning attack is a cyber-attack where an attacker sends false Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) messages to link their Media Access Control (MAC) address with a legitimate Internet Protocol (IP) address, intercepting and manipulating network traffic. Birthday attacks are a cryptographic exploit that leverages the probability of two different inputs producing the same hash value. Attackers use this likelihood to compromise hash functions and forge digital signatures or certificates. Buffer overflow attacks occur when a program writes more data to a memory buffer than it can hold, causing excess data to overflow into adjacent memory locations. This vulnerability can be exploited to execute malicious code or crash the system.

Correct answer: An automated mechanism that prevents the disclosure of sensitive information

A data loss prevention (DLP) system monitors for and prevents potential disclosures of sensitive information. For example, if Social Security numbers are detected in a document, the DLP system may prevent them from being emailed or printed.

Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) is a distinct technology from DLP. It protects stored data using a few different techniques, such as mirroring and parity. In the cloud, there are technologies that emulate RAID capability, categorized as erasure coding and data dispersion. The former is similar to RAID 5 and the latter to RAID 0.

There may be many names for specific backup systems, but DLP is not one of them. 

DLP can reduce risks related to data privacy and data security breaches and can therefore reduce the risk of compliance violations. However, it focuses on prevention, not disaster recovery.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Rivest, Shamir, & Adleman (RSA)

Rivest, Shamir, & Adleman (RSA) is an asymmetric algorithm that uses public and private keys. RSA is often used to distribute symmetric encryption keys because asymmetric encryption is computationally expensive and can’t be used to efficiently encrypt large amounts of data. When using asymmetric algorithms like RSA, if a message is encrypted using the private key, it can only be decrypted using the public key; this rule also applies in reverse. If a message is encrypted with the public key, it can only be decrypted using the private key.

Diffie-Hellman (DH) is an asymmetric algorithm. Mr. Diffie and Mr. Hellman wrote a paper in 1976 that theorized public and private keys. However, the algorithm they came up with does not work that way. It is an algorithm for the purpose of exchanging a symmetric key only. They were unsuccessful in finding the math to use public and private keys. RSA did that in 1977. AES and Blowfish are both symmetric algorithms that are used to protect the confidentiality of data, voice, or video.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Nonce

A Nonce is a random number or value generated by the authentication server. When a client requests to authenticate, the server will reply with the Nonce; this is often called the challenge. The client will combine the Nonce with a predefined password and use a hashing algorithm to generate a response. The server will use the same Nonce and predefined password to create a hash. If the hash generated by the client and server match, the server will authenticate the client. Each Nonce can only be used once and helps prevent replay attacks.

A hashing algorithm is run against a piece of data/voice/video/password. The hashing algorithm will produce a fixed size response often called a hash or a message digest. The hashing algorithms are public. It is possible for anyone to hash a piece of data or rehash it so it does not provide any protection against replay.

A one-time pad is an encryption method. It involves a message encrypted using a unique key that is as long as the message and is never used again. One-time pads are provably unbreakable by brute force attacks. There are other methods of attack that can be successful against it though.

A cipher is another name of an encryption algorithm. These are used to protect the confidentiality of data/voice/video, especially if they are symmetric in nature.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP)

Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) is a framework for authentication rather than a standalone authentication protocol. EAP is used to negotiate the best authentication method that both a client and server agree on and can include smartcards, tokens, and biometrics. EAP can support these different authentication methods, and it can support one or two factors of authentication. Protected Extensible Authentication Protocol (PEAP) is similar to EAP but is encapsulated in a TLS session using a server-side certificate.

Challenge-Handshake Authentication Protocol (CHAP) only supports a password—similar to the older Password Authentication Protocol (PAP).

Single Sign-On (SSO) does not define what kind of authentication methods can be used. Since the question actually specifies different methods, EAP is the better answer because that is the distinguishing feature of EAP.

result.prompt: Which of the following is the only approved method for sanitizing Top Secret media?

subtopics.name: 2.1 Identify and classify information and assets
2.2 Establish information and asset handling requirements
2.3 Provision information and assets securely
2.4 Manage data lifecycle
2.5 Ensure appropriate asset retention (e.g., End of Life (EOL), End of Support)
2.6 Determine data security controls and compliance requirements

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Destruction

Destruction is the most thorough form of sanitization and is, therefore, the only approved method of sanitizing Top Secret data. If a drive is properly destroyed, e.g. shredded to small enough pieces, it is the most effective way to destroy data.

Degaussing is used to alter the magnetic state of a magnetic drive, e.g. Hard Disk Drive (HDD). It renders the drive useless and fairly effectively destroys all data. It would take specialized tools in a lab environment to ever recover anything off of a degaussed drive. The likelihood of recovery of any data is near zero percent. If destruction was not a possible answer to this question, degaussing would be an acceptable answer, but it does not work on Solid State Drives (SSD). Since the question does not specify HDD vs SSD, destruction is a better answer here.

Clear is defined in the United States (US) National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-88 as a method that “Applies logical techniques to sanitize data in all user-addressable storage locations for protection against simple non-invasive data recovery techniques; typically applied through the standard Read and Write commands to the storage device, such as by rewriting with a new value or using a menu option to reset the device to the factory state (where rewriting is not supported).” It is not as effective as purging or the destruction of a drive.

Deleting, erasing, clearing, and then degaussing are many steps, but the process is still not as good as proper physical destruction.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Something you have

The three main types of authentication factors include:

  • Something You Have: Possession-based factors include smartcards, hardware tokens, smartphones, or a USB drive. A One-Time Password (OTP) is sent to or generated by a physical device, making it a possession-based factor.
  • Something You Know:  Knowledge-based factors include passwords, PINs, passphrases, and security questions.
  • Something You Are: Inherence-based factors include fingerprints, facial recognition, retina and iris scans, palmprints, and voice recognition.

Somewhere you are is a least-used factor that uses IP addresses or geolocation to determine if a login attempt comes from a logical or trusted location.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: A device that generates unique passwords in set intervals

Hardware tokens that generate passwords without a challenge-response process are known as synchronous password tokens. Synchronous tokens are time-based and synchronized with an authentication server. They generate a new password periodically, such as every 30 or 60 seconds. This requires the token and the server to maintain an accurate time. Tokens provide multi-factor authentication.

A device that generates passwords using a challenge number is an asynchronous token that is considered challenge/response in nature. There is no name for a device that generates passwords at a random time. There is also no name for a list of passwords that are used once and in order.

Correct answer: Cryptology

Cryptology is the science of secure communications and is the study of both cryptography and cryptanalysis.

Cryptography is the study of encryption and decryption techniques to protect the transmission and storage of data, voice, and video. Cryptanalysis is the study of methods to break encryption technologies. This can be referred to as ethical hacking, as it is necessary for the good guys to test the security level of the encryption algorithms that corporations are using to protect their data, voice, and video. Hacking is a term that has gone through several evolutions of use. Originally it meant that a software developer was very good at their job and they could take someone else’s code and make it do even more. Then it evolved to mean bad people who are trying to find holes in the software to be able to get the software to do more than it was supposed to for evil purposes.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Tabletop

Testing disaster response plans is essential to ensure that they are effective and nothing is missed. Testing can be performed in various ways, including:

  • Read-through/Tabletop: A read-through or tabletop exercise involves reading through and role-playing the disaster response plan. This is the cheapest, least disruptive, and least realistic form of testing. This would not involve an employee driving to the alternate site as part of the exercise.
  • Walkthrough: In a walkthrough, the team physically performs the actions described in the plan (unless they would disrupt operations). This can build familiarity and help identify parts of the plan that are impossible or require additional resources.
  • Simulation: In a simulation like a fire drill, the team is given a scenario and tasked with responding to it. This is more realistic than a walkthrough but can be more disruptive to operations since tasks are actually completed.
  • Parallel Test: Parallel tests perform normal business operations at an alternate as well as the primary site. This ensures that the alternate site can complete its duties while minimizing the potential impact on normal operations.
  • Full-Interruption Test: A full-interruption test actually switches operations over from the primary to the recovery site. This is more disruptive and risky than a parallel test but actually verifies that the organization’s failover processes work.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Hire a qualified third party to conduct a security assessment

Security assessments are used to determine an organization's security posture. They should be conducted by qualified individuals who know how to properly assess controls and decide whether they are sufficient or not. When possible, these assessments should be undertaken by third parties to eliminate conflicts of interest. Once the assessment report is delivered to management, they can make the recommendations outlined in the report.

Performing a SOC 2 audit in particular could be a great idea. However, this specific audit should be included in the correct answer. Conducting a security assessment is a more broad answer.

Talking to the security team would be a good idea. The problem with asking for a list of recommendations, though, is that they could be biased. Using the Delphi method does help the process by making it anonymous, but the question is asking what would be the best action. Having a third party conduct a security assessment of some sort is best because of the impartiality that a third party should bring to the task.

result.prompt: What security device is employed to filter traffic between two computer networks?

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
4.2 Secure network components
4.3 Implement secure communication channels according to design

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Firewall

Firewalls are essential tools in managing and controlling network traffic. A firewall is a network device used to filter traffic and is generally deployed between a private network and the internet. However, a firewall can be deployed anywhere segmentation and filtering are needed.

Though a router can bridge communications between a private network and the internet, it is not designed to filter traffic like a firewall. It does have some basic filtering through the use of access control lists (ACLs) which could be considered a basic firewall. However, firewall is a more straightforward answer, which makes it the better answer here.

A switch is designed to forward traffic, usually between local area network (LAN) cables. It usually forwards traffic because of knowledge of media access control (MAC) addresses. It does not filter; it only forwards.

A virtual local area network (VLAN) can logically isolate networks, but it does not provide the same filtering capabilities as a firewall.

Scrum focuses on empirical feedback, team self-management, and adequately tested product increments within short iterations.

A software development methodology is a framework used to structure, plan, and control the process of developing an information system. Examples are Waterfall, Spiral, Agile, Scrum, Extreme Programming, and Joint Application Development.

The purpose of job rotation is to act as a deterrent and a detection tool. The primary benefits of job rotation are:

  • Provides peer review (2): When a new employee rotates into a role, they must review the previous employee’s work, which can reveal mistakes or irregularities.
  • Reduces fraud (3): Job rotation discourages long-term concealment of fraudulent activities and increases the chance of discovery when duties change hands.
  • Enables cross-training (4): Rotation ensures multiple employees are capable of performing critical job functions, reducing reliance on any single individual.

Improving employee relationships (1) is not a primary control objective of job rotation and may even complicate relationships when errors are discovered.

Split knowledge (5) is a preventive control, often applied to cryptographic key management, and is unrelated to job rotation.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Buffer overflow

A buffer overflow attack is most commonly applied to exploit this weakness. A buffer overflow occurs when an application buffer is populated with data that exceeds the capacity allocated to it, causing the excess data to "overflow" into adjacent memory (thereby overwriting it with the excess data). Buffer overflow attacks exploit this to overwrite memory locations that contain application code with malicious code that is incorporated into the excess data.

Integer overflows are similar to buffer overflows but deal specifically with numeric values overflowing a predefined capacity.

A memory leak is the waste condition that results from an application that fails to release memory it has allocated but no longer needs. A memory leak is not itself an attack type but can sometimes be exploited by malicious actors performing denial-of-service attacks.

Output encoding is not an attack type but an application security technique used to prevent attacks. It converts certain characters within website form inputs (e.g., apostrophes) into their HTML character entity reference equivalents (e.g., "&apos") to ensure these characters are processed as data (and not misinterpreted as programming syntax).

result.prompt: What type of cyber threat is BEST described as thousands of individual computers used together to attack a target?

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
4.2 Secure network components
4.3 Implement secure communication channels according to design

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Botnet

A botnet is made up of thousands (or millions) of computers that give the attacker (the bot-herder) the ability to control them. A computer that is part of a botnet is called a zombie or bot. Data transmissions between the bot-herder and the individual zombies are called command and control (C&C) traffic. Botnets can be used in distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks or brute-force attacks. 

A C&C server is often used to control a botnet but is not the name of the threat. 

A smurf attack sends broadcast Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) echo request packets (aka PING packets) that spoof the source Internet Protocol (IP) address as the target victim’s IP address. 

A honeynet is a network that has been set up to distract a bad actor. It should have a lot of alerts that are sent to the Network Operations Center (NOC) or the Security Operations Center (SOC) so that the incident response (IR) teams can take immediate action to ensure the bad actor does not get into the business's real systems.

result.prompt: Of the following access control models, which allows the data owner to determine how subjects and objects interact with each other?

subtopics.name: 5.1 Control physical and logical access to assets
5.2 Design identification and authentication strategy (e.g., people, devices, and services)
5.3 Federated identity with a third-party service
5.4 Implement and manage authorization mechanisms
5.5 Manage the identity and access provisioning lifecycle
5.6 Implement authentication systems

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Discretionary

In Discretionary Access Control (DAC) models, the data owner is responsible for assigning permissions for the object. Each object has a data owner, and these owners determine permissions. The data owner can also audit, edit, and delete an object. It is up to the owner's discretion who should have access and at what levels.

The other access control models listed involve more than just the owner's wishes. Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) uses attributes such as source Internet Protocol (IP) address, time of day, and condition of the source machine (is it patched, etc.). Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) uses the grouping of users into roles such as doctor, nurse, or administrator to determine the level of access to grant the user. Mandatory Access Control (MAC) relies on the classification of the object, the clearance of the subject, and the corporate policy for the intersection of the levels to determine the appropriate level of access. Bell-LaPadula is a great example of the logic that should be clarified within the corporate data policy.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Constrained interface

An organization may use various means to manage authorization on a system, including constrained interface. A constrained interface modifies the user interface based on a subject’s privileges. If a user doesn’t have the right to click a button, then the button is not shown or is grayed-out.

In implicit deny, the system has a list of authorized users (allowlist), and anyone not on the list is denied access.

Access control matrices map combinations of subjects and objects to their associated permissions, rights, and privileges. An Access Control List (ACL) is a row in this matrix associated with a single object.

Capability lists are like ACLs focused on a subject, describing all the things that they are permitted to do.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Digital certificates

Digital certificates contain public keys that belong to someone or something (e.g. a web server). The standard package that holds the public keys is the ITU-TSS X.509 format. There are several other fields within the certificate such as the subject’s name and the Certificate Authorities (CA) signature. The CA is the trusted source of certificates. They (human and computer combined) are charged with knowing for sure who the key will belong to and then publishing the X.509 certificate.

A digital signature is created when the subject (someone or something) encrypts something (a.k.a. signs something) by encrypting it with their private key. What is normally encrypted is the hash of the data that it relates to. The private key should never be in someone else’s possession so that the digital signature truly means something. Public Key Infrastructure is the correct term, not private key infrastructure. The public key can be shared with anyone.

result.prompt:
Acme Inc. must run legacy Windows XP computers for a specific business workflow. Previously the computers were connected to the internet, and because Windows XP has known vulnerabilities, one of the computers was compromised. 

To reduce the risk of threat actors compromising those computers going forward, Acme Inc. no longer allows them to be connected to the internet. This is an example of what type of risk response?

1.2 Understand and apply security concepts
1.3 Evaluate and apply security governance principles
1.4 Understand legal, regulatory, and compliance issues that pertain to information security in a holistic context

1.6 Develop, document, and implement security policy, standards, procedures, and guidelines

1.8 Contribute to and enforce personnel security policies and procedures

1.10 Understand and apply threat modeling concepts and methodologies
1.11 Apply supply chain risk management (SCRM) concepts
1.12 Establish and maintain a security awareness, education, and training program

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Mitigation

These are the possible responses to risk:

  • Mitigation: Implement security controls to reduce or eliminate the risk. In this case, Acme Inc. reduced risk by disconnecting the Windows XP computers from the internet. 
  • Acceptance: Accept the potential consequences and costs of the risk to the organization. Leaving the Windows XP computers as is would have been risk acceptance.  
  • Assignment/transfer: Transfer the responsibility for a risk to someone else, such as an insurer. Purchasing cyber insurance for the Windows XP computers would have been risk transfer. 
  • Avoidance: Avoid taking the action that creates the risk. Ending the use of the Windows XP computers and associated workflow would have been risk avoidance.

result.prompt: Which of the following is a type of firewall designed to identify whether a packet is valid within the context of the overall conversation?

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
4.2 Secure network components
4.3 Implement secure communication channels according to design

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Stateful

A stateful firewall monitors the current state of network connections and blocks packets that are invalid in context (OSI Layers 3 and 4).

A static packet filtering, screening router, or stateless firewall evaluates each packet independently based on its header fields (OSI Layer 3).

A circuit-level firewall ensures that the TCP handshake was completed and conceals information about the protected network. (Theoretically OSI Layer 5, but also looks at TCP data at Layer 4.) SOCKS proxies are examples of circuit firewalls.

An application-level firewall understands application-specific traffic and can filter traffic accordingly (OSI Layer 7). A Web Application Firewall (WAF) is an example of an application-level firewall.

The users opened the emails and attachments, which caused a breach of some sensitive information. result.explanation:
Correct answer: Regular training for employees 

Training and education are the best ways to help users avoid falling prey to social engineering attacks of any kind, including phishing.

Attackers can still manipulate an untrained employee into divulging a password over the phone. So, requiring MFA will not necessarily stop a social engineering attack.

Additional identity verification controls should be implemented before passwords are distributed over the phone. Social engineering attacks that occur over the phone are known as vishing or pre-texting.

Classifying information with clear rules for its use at each level is critical, but it does not help a user avoid falling for a phishing email. It may help them understand data sensitivity and be more careful about discussing it casually.

6.2 Conduct security control testing
6.3 Collect security process data (e.g., technical and administrative)
6.4 Analyze test output and generate report
6.5 Conduct or facilitate security audits

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Penetration test

Security testing comes in a variety of different forms. Some of the main types include:

  • Penetration Testing: Penetration testing includes vulnerability assessments but also attempts to exploit the vulnerabilities that they discover. Additionally, they involve more manual testing than a fully-automated vulnerability scan.
  • Vulnerability Assessments: Vulnerability assessments use automated tools to identify vulnerabilities within an organization’s systems, including networks, web applications, and databases. Typically these check an application against the list of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) to identify known issues. These vulnerabilities are scored using the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS), which helps in identifying how severe the vulnerability is.
  • Breach and Attack Simulations (BAS): BAS platforms are designed to perform automated penetration testing. They introduce indicators of compromise (IoCs) into the system — malicious files, C2 traffic, etc. — and check if the corporate security controls identify it.
  • Compliance Checks: Compliance checks verify that an organization implements the security controls required by applicable regulations and that they are functional. These tests can also be automated.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Purpose limitation

The European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is intended to protect an individual's personal information held by corporations. The GDPR uses several provisions to achieve its goals. The purpose limitation provision requires documentation and disclosure of the reasons data is being processed.

The lawfulness, fairness, and transparency provision requires a legal basis for personal information processing, prohibits processing data in a way that is detrimental to data subjects, and requires data-processing-related activity to be transparent.

The integrity and confidentiality provision requires security controls to protect personal information from unauthorized access.

Storage limitation is a requirement to keep data for only as long as it is needed. This provision is the source of the well-known "right to be forgotten."

Grid computing is similar to clustering, but individual nodes do not trust each other and can join and leave at will. Grid computing is generally distributed across hundreds or thousands of nodes across the internet. Nodes check in when they have available system resources and contribute to grid processing. Grid processing typically spans multiple organizations rather than focusing on the goals of a single organization. 

A group of nodes that are logically viewed as one is not real; neither is central processing distributed across multiple cores. Multiple cores exist within most computers today, which is not viewed as "central" processing.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Detective

These are the main types of security controls:

  • Detective: Detective controls help to identify that an incident is occurring. CCTV, audit trails, and honeypots are examples of detective controls. Audit logs track user activity and provide records that can be used to detect a problem.
  • Preventive: Preventive controls are designed to stop an incident from happening. Fences, locks, and access controls are examples of preventive controls.
  • Corrective: Corrective controls fix problems after a security incident occurs. Anti-malware that removes an infection and an auto-close arm on a door are examples of corrective controls.
  • Recovery: Recovery controls restore normal operations after an incident to a greater extent than corrective ones. Backups and server clusters are examples of recovery controls.
  • Deterrent: Deterrent controls attempt to discourage an incident from occurring. Corporate policies and security cameras are examples of deterrent controls.
  • Compensating: A compensating control is used as a replacement when the preferred control is unusable. For example, a company renting an office in a building may put locks on the doors when it can't build a fence.

"Forensic" and "lagging" are not standard types of security controls.

5.2 Design identification and authentication strategy (e.g., people, devices, and services)
5.3 Federated identity with a third-party service
5.4 Implement and manage authorization mechanisms
5.5 Manage the identity and access provisioning lifecycle
5.6 Implement authentication systems

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Mandatory Access Control

A system that employs Mandatory Access Control (MAC) uses classifications and labels to define user access. Every resource is classified with a label, and users cannot access resources unless they have an equal or greater clearance level. MAC is widely used in government and military environments. MAC is often referred to as a lattice-based model because it looks like a garden lattice with well-defined boundaries when it is represented on paper.

Discretionary Access Control (DAC) allows the data owner to control and define access to objects. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) maps a subject’s role with their needed operations and tasks. Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) makes decisions based on attributes for either the subject, object, or actions.

Micki is the plant manager of a manufacturing company. She proceeds to log in to her workstation using a username and password.

What BEST describes the role of the username?

subtopics.name: 5.1 Control physical and logical access to assets
5.2 Design identification and authentication strategy (e.g., people, devices, and services)
5.3 Federated identity with a third-party service
5.4 Implement and manage authorization mechanisms
5.5 Manage the identity and access provisioning lifecycle
5.6 Implement authentication systems

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Identification

Identification is claiming or professing an identity. A subject must provide an identity to a system to start the authentication, authorization, and accountability processes. Providing an identity might entail typing a username, swiping a smart card, waving a token device, speaking a phrase, etc.

Authentication is providing information to verify the claim in the identification step. There are three main factors of authentication: something you know, something you have, and something you are. 

Authorization is the process of granting (or denying) permissions once the identification is proven, such as read, write, execute, or tag. 

Credentials include both the username and password. While the username is part of Micki's credentials, identification is the more specific and therefore better answer.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Double door installation

Double door installations, or mantraps, force individuals into a small room with an ingress and egress door. Before the person can exit through the egress door, the ingress door must be closed and locked. If the individual is authorized, the egress door will unlock, and they can proceed. If they are not authorized, both doors remain locked until a security guard or police officer arrives and escorts them off the property or arrests them for trespassing. It is common for mantraps to have a weight scale across the floor to ensure only one person is in the room at a time.

Identification badges, bollards, and administrative policy would be additional controls, but mantraps are considered the most effective at preventing piggybacking.

Training employees frequently will ensure better security for the organization as a whole. Generally speaking, employees are the greatest threat to an organization. This is usually due to accidents, lack of knowledge, and specifically, cyberattacks such as phishing attempts that could be thwarted with regular education.

Investing a lot of money may help, but at some point, the return on investment won't be great if employees aren't trained on how to use new devices and mis-configure them anyway. Understanding how to use tools and how to avoid becoming victims involves knowing both the technical and human sides of security. result.explanation:
Correct answer: Destruction

Destruction involves disintegrating or otherwise destroying data in a physical manner. This could include destroying hard drives or disintegrating paper files that have sensitive data.

Degaussing clears data on a drive using magnetization to impact the magnetic field associated with the data but could allow for the platters to be installed on a new drive and data to be read. Erasing only deletes the directory link to the file, not the actual data. Purging involves multiple rewrites over data to make it unrecoverable, typically combined with another method such as degaussing. While appearing to be a secure method of ensuring data is unrecoverable, this form of destruction is not considered safe by the US government, and top-secret material is destroyed instead.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: One-time pad

Gilbert Vernam invented the One-Time Pad (OTP) in 1917 and it is sometimes referred to as the Vernam Cipher. A one-time pad requires a completely random key that is the same length as the message. Each bit of the message and the key are exclusive-OR (XOR) together. The resulting ciphertext is considered unbreakable by brute force as long as the key remains secure. For a one-time pad to be implemented correctly, keys cannot be reused and must truly be random.

One-time pad requirements:

  • Keys must be genuinely random values
  • Keys can only be used one time
  • Keys must be exchanged securely
  • The sender and receiver must keep the keys secure
  • The key must be the same length as the message

The Vigenère cipher was invented by Blaise de Vigenère in the 16th century. It is a polyalphabetic cipher. Side note, it was first described by Bellaso in 1553. Brief studies of the old algorithms, such as Vernam, Ceasar, and Vigenère, can make learning the new algorithms a bit easier. We have two concepts that we primarily use, and have used for centuries, and they are substitution and transposition. Both Vernman and Vigenère are substitution ciphers.

The DES algorithm was adapted from Dr. Horst Feistel's algorithm, known as Lucifer. It was the first widely adopted symmetric encryption algorithm in today's computing environment. It was eventually replaced by triple DES. They are both outdated now and have been replaced by the Advanced Encryption Standard. DES and AES use both substitution and transposition.

Blowfish was invented by Bruce Schneir in 1993. He intended for it to replace DES, but now he recommends his algorithm Twofish. These two are both substitution and transposition.

All of these algorithms are symmetric in nature.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Data owner

A data owner is the party responsible for directly or indirectly managing the life cycle of a set of data, excluding modifying policies already set within the company.

Generally, data controllers set policies and are the senior managers in a company. A data owner then decides who will be given access to that data based on prior-determined policies and maintains the data throughout the life cycle, including classifying the data. A data processor, under the European Union (EU) General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), processes data, which includes something like running payroll or holding data, on behalf of the company the data belongs to. The data processor cannot be a person from within the company. 

A data architect designs the data structures and related systems in a way that meets business objectives.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: FAR

Biometric authentication systems can produce various types of errors, including false positives, which are false acceptances or Type 2 errors when a system incorrectly authenticates an unauthorized user. The False Acceptance Rate (FAR) is calculated as the ratio of false acceptances to valid authentications.

False negatives are false rejections or Type 1 errors when a system fails to authenticate a legitimate user. The ratio of false rejections to valid authentications is the False Rejection Rate (FRR).

The Crossover Error Rate (CER) or Equal Error Rate (ERR) is when the FRR equals the FAR.

result.prompt:
An organization has just conducted a vulnerability test via a third party and found that all its PS-100 point-of-sale systems have a major vulnerability. 

The data at rest in the point-of-sale systems is not encrypted, and data masking is not done until receipts are printed. The organization contacted the vendor about the issue and wants to reach out to competitors in the area who may use similar systems to protect their customers as well.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: To prevent the information from getting into the wrong hands

The organization should keep its customers' information from getting into the wrong hands by not telling the public or even those in their industry until the situation has been resolved. The organization has an ethical duty to inform the vendor immediately and allow reasonable time for the incident to be resolved. If the organization takes a different course of action, it may give the competitor or another potential threat actor an opportunity to conduct an attack that affects the organization.

While it may seem nice to tell customers firsthand and let them know how the company plans to resolve the issue, customers could spread this information or may simply lack the technical knowledge to understand it. 

As the question states, the vulnerability is considered serious because it affects all the organization's point-of-sale systems, and unauthorized access could pose a major threat to customer data, resulting in potential legal and financial issues for the organization. Therefore, it is unlikely that the vulnerability score is too low to act.

Although there is no threat at this time, that is not a valid reason for a organization to avoid being proactive.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Bell-LaPadula

Bell-LaPadula was the first mathematical model of a Multilevel Security (MLS) policy. The concept of MLS is the idea that a system would have multiple levels of classification in the same system. Access control philosophies can be organized into models that define approaches to security issues. The Take-Grant model, the Bell-LaPadula model, and the Biba model are examples of different access control models.

Bell-LaPadula was released in 1976 by the US government to provide for better confidentiality. The Biba model was released in 1975, but it addresses integrity. The Clark & Wilson model is from 1987 and also addresses integrity. The Brewer and Nash model is from 1989 and its primary focus is on the confidentiality of data.

result.explanation:

The cost and lack of familiarity with an organization's systems can be a drawback to third-party audits. For example, someone who is unfamiliar with the systems will take longer to conduct an audit. Additionally, they may require additional resources that an internal employee wouldn't need, which may include having someone show them around the building or familiarizing the auditor with the structure of networks.

Since a third party has no vested interest in the company they're auditing, it's fair to say the auditor would be impartial during the audit. With that said, they would have less of a reason to not be transparent with whoever they may be auditing. Third-party auditors are just as qualified as anyone to audit, so again, there is no reason not to trust their practices or the accuracy of results. After all, they may be conducting the audit on behalf of a major auditor. Logically, conflicts of interest would be vetted to avoid any of the aforementioned worries.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Dialogue control

The session layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model is used primarily to track application dialogue. The session layer (Layer 5) establishes, coordinates, and terminates communication sessions between applications. Examples of session layer protocols are Remote Procedure Call (RPC) and Network File System (NFS).

Routing occurs at the network layer using the Internet Protocol (IP) version 4 or 6 (IPv4, IPv6) addresses within the routers. Framing is a term used at layer two of the Open System Interconnect (OSI) model, the data link layer. Framing refers to the packaging of the payload with a frame header and frame trailer. The frame header would include an address used for forwarding the frames in the right direction. In Ethernet, the address is the Media Access Control (MAC) address. Formatting is a more general term. It does not apply within the OSI model at any specific layer.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Network Address Translation (NAT)

Network Address Translation (NAT) is used to translate between two Internet Protocol (IP) addresses. Typically, NAT is enabled on a router connected to the internet. The router translates all internal private IP addresses to a public IP address when outgoing connections are made and translates the return traffic to the private IP address.

Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA) is used to assign a network device an address if one is not dynamically assigned by a DHCP server or statically assigned on the system. 

Intra-Site Automatic Tunnel Addressing Protocol (ISATAP) is a protocol used to transmit IPv6 packets when the systems are dual-stack, meaning they support both IPv4 and IPv6. 

Generic Routing Encapsulation (GRE) is a tunneling protocol that can encapsulate a wide variety of protocols. It is a method of protecting data in transmission. That data can be what a user is transmitting or what a server is transmitting in the course of a normal workday. It will not hide any IP address.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Internal audits can be used to demonstrate compliance against an external standard for government or industry compliance

Internal audits should not be used to demonstrate compliance against an external standard for government or industry compliance. This is because internal audits present a conflict of interest. An organization should use a third party to audit them when audit reports are used for compliance reasons.

Internal audits should be used in preparation for an external or third party audit. Internal audits allow an organization to test gaps and continuously improve its security program. Regular internal audits also show due care and due diligence.

result.prompt: Which networking method is used to map internal Internet Protocol (IP) addresses to external IP addresses?

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
4.2 Secure network components
4.3 Implement secure communication channels according to design

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Network Address Translation (NAT)

Network Address Translation (NAT) is a method of remapping one IP address space into another by modifying the network address information in the IP header of packets while they are in transit across a router. NAT operates at the network layer of the Open System Interconnection (OSI) model.

Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) maps the IP address to the hardware-based Media Access Control (MAC) address. This occurs when the IP protocol is sent over Ethernet.

Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) is a protocol used to assign an IP address, dynamically, to devices as they are connected to a network. The connection could be physical or wireless.

Internet Protocol Message Protocol (ICMP) is a protocol used by network administrators. ICMP is used to PING devices to determine if they are connected and responsive. If they do not respond it is possible to then use traceroute to determine how far the communication can pass through the network. This allows the troubleshooting to begin at a certain point.

8.2 Identify and apply security controls in software development ecosystems
8.3 Assess the effectiveness of software security
8.4 Assess security impact of acquired software

result.explanation:
Correct answer: A television with a broken backlight

Simply put, a television with a broken backlight does not meet the requirements for a runtime environment. A runtime environment must be an environment in which all hardware and software components are available to fully operate.

A gaming computer, virtual machine, and high-latency game server all meet the criteria for a runtime environment. It doesn't matter if their resources are limited, so long as they are fully capable of running.

result.prompt: Acme Inc. wants to reduce the risk of MAC flooding on its local networks. Which of the following would BEST address this risk?

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
4.2 Secure network components
4.3 Implement secure communication channels according to design

result.explanation:
Correct answer: MAC limiting on a managed switch

MAC flooding is a type of Layer 2 (data link layer) attack. It works by attempting to flood a switch with randomized MAC addresses and overload the content addressable memory (CAM) table.

A managed switch operates at Layer 2, and the MAC limiting feature restricts how many MAC addresses the switch will accept from a given port. Therefore, it is well suited to address MAC flooding risk. 

Packet inspection on a network intrusion detection system (NIDS) would not directly address MAC flooding.

Network routers operate at Layer 3 (network layer), and therefore the answers that use a router are incorrect.

result.prompt: Which type of network discovery scan opens a full connection with a remote system on a specific port?

subtopics.name: 6.1 Design and validate assessment, test, and audit strategies
6.2 Conduct security control testing
6.3 Collect security process data (e.g., technical and administrative)
6.4 Analyze test output and generate report
6.5 Conduct or facilitate security audits

result.explanation:
Correct answer: TCP connect scan

Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) connect scanning opens a full connection, meaning that the scanner replies with an ACK to complete the TCP three-way handshake. This type of scan is usually selected when the user does not have privileges to run half-open scans.

A TCP SYN scan is incorrect because it is a half-open scan and only sends a packet with the SYN flag set. TCP ACK scan is incorrect because it is also a half-open scan and only sends a packet with the ACK flag set. Xmas scan is incorrect because it does not open a full connection and, instead, sends a packet with the FIN, PSH, and URG flags set.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Policy

A security policy is a high-level description of an organization's security requirements.

Standards define required activities that are designed to help an organization fulfill its policy goals.

Procedures are step-by-step descriptions of how a member of the organization should achieve a security goal.

Guidelines provide recommendations about how to do something if no specific standard exists.

result.prompt: Of the following, what technique is MOST likely to prevent the execution of non-genuine software by ensuring that users and administrators can verify the program is from a trusted developer?

subtopics.name: 8.1 Understand and integrate security in the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC)
8.2 Identify and apply security controls in software development ecosystems
8.3 Assess the effectiveness of software security
8.4 Assess security impact of acquired software
8.5 Define and apply secure coding guidelines and standards

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Code signing

Code signing is when a software developer signs their code using a private key. Systems can be configured to execute only applications and code that a trusted developer has signed.

Code signing provides integrity for software. However, it does not necessarily mean the software is safe. If attackers can inject malicious code into a software repository that the trusted developer signs, it will be trusted by systems that require code to be signed. In 2019 and 2020, hackers successfully injected malicious code into a product named Orion created by SolarWinds that was signed and trusted.

A code review should be performed by software developers through the process of creating software. However, it does not have anything to do with execution or running of software in a production environment. 

Code versioning is also done by software developers to maintain their code, but it simply labels each new version of an application. These versions still need to be signed to allow users to verify they came from a trusted developer.

Application allowlisting (formerly whitelisting) is related to the execution of software but not so-called genuine software. An allowlist is a list of applications that a user may add or run on their systems, but non-genuine software could be in that list.

result.prompt: Which one-time password (OTP) algorithm generates a new code upon each login attempt rather than waiting a specific amount of time before changing the code?

subtopics.name: 5.1 Control physical and logical access to assets
5.2 Design identification and authentication strategy (e.g., people, devices, and services)
5.3 Federated identity with a third-party service
5.4 Implement and manage authorization mechanisms
5.5 Manage the identity and access provisioning lifecycle
5.6 Implement authentication systems

result.explanation:
Correct answer: HOTP

One-time passwords (OTPs) are six-to-eight-digit numbers used as part of a multifactor authentication scheme. They can be generated in two ways:

  • HMAC-based one-time password (HOTP): HOTPs are generated using an incrementing counter. Each authentication attempt using an HOTP causes both the authenticator and the server to regenerate it.
  • Time-based one-time password (TOTP): TOTPs are regenerated by the authenticator and the server at regular intervals. With synchronized clocks, this ensures that both devices have the same code at the same time without needing to communicate after initial setup.

NOTP and IOTP are fabricated acronyms.

result.prompt: Under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which of the following roles is DIRECTLY responsible for determining the purpose and means of processing personal data?

subtopics.name: 2.1 Identify and classify information and assets
2.2 Establish information and asset handling requirements
2.3 Provision information and assets securely
2.4 Manage data lifecycle
2.5 Ensure appropriate asset retention (e.g., End of Life (EOL), End of Support)
2.6 Determine data security controls and compliance requirements

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Data controller

The data controller is the role defined by the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) as having direct responsibility for determining the purpose and means of processing personal data. This includes deciding why data is collected, determining how it will be used, and ensuring compliance with GDPR requirements. Data controllers are legally accountable for data handling practices and for protecting individuals’ privacy rights.

The data custodian is a role commonly used in organizational data governance models, but it is not defined under GDPR. Data custodians are typically responsible for the technical and operational management of data—such as storage, access controls, and backups—based on the instructions of the data controller.

The data processor, which is defined under GDPR, is responsible for processing data on behalf of the data controller, but does not decide how or why the data is processed.

A data subject is the individual the data is about.

result.prompt: A biometric authentication system has a high Type I error rate. This indicates it has a high number of what?

subtopics.name: 5.1 Control physical and logical access to assets
5.2 Design identification and authentication strategy (e.g., people, devices, and services)
5.3 Federated identity with a third-party service
5.4 Implement and manage authorization mechanisms
5.5 Manage the identity and access provisioning lifecycle
5.6 Implement authentication systems

result.explanation:
Correct answer: False rejections 

Biometric authentication systems can produce various types of errors:

  • False negatives: False rejections or Type 1 errors are when a system fails to authenticate a legitimate user. The ratio of false rejections to valid authentications is the false rejection rate (FRR).
  • False positives: False acceptances, or Type 2 errors, occur when a system incorrectly authenticates an unauthorized user. The false acceptance rate (FAR) is the ratio of false acceptances to valid authentications.

True negatives and true positives are not errors.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Kerberos

Kerberos is an authentication system commonly used to implement SSO on internal networks. ASREPRoast is a type of Kerberos exploit that aims to identify accounts without preauthentication so the threat actor can discover the client's password offline. 

RADIUS and TACACS+ are remote access protocols for corporate networks. SAML is a standard commonly used to implement SSO systems. These are not targeted in an ASREPRoast exploit.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Permission

Some key terms in IAM include:

  • Permissions: Permissions define what a user is permitted to do with a particular object, such as read/write access for a file.
  • Right: Rights define the ability to take a particular action on an object.
  • Privilege: Privilege combines rights and elevated permissions. An administrator-level account has elevated permissions and the right to act on almost any object on a computer.

An attribute is something that describes a subject or object.

result.prompt: Which of the following access control models allows the data owner to define access to resources?

subtopics.name: 5.1 Control physical and logical access to assets
5.2 Design identification and authentication strategy (e.g., people, devices, and services)
5.3 Federated identity with a third-party service
5.4 Implement and manage authorization mechanisms
5.5 Manage the identity and access provisioning lifecycle
5.6 Implement authentication systems

result.explanation:
Correct answer: DAC

A system that employs discretionary access control (DAC) allows the owner to control and define access to objects. All objects have owners, and access is at the discretion or decision of the owner. Objects are files, folders, applications, functions, etc.

Mandatory access control (MAC) uses data classification and user clearances to determine the level of access granted. The system is programmed with the corporation's policy regarding classifications and clearances and how they relate to each other. The system then enforces these rules. It eliminates the discretion of the owner in granting access. The data or system owner would identify who needs access.

Role-based access control (RBAC) maps a subject’s role to their needed operations and tasks. It reduces the workload by identifying the access that a role, such as a nurse or doctor, requires as opposed to identifying the access each nurse requires.

Attribute-based access control (ABAC) makes decisions based on attributes of the subject, object, or actions. It has been used in networking under the name network access control (NAC) and is now commonly used in the cloud.

result.prompt: Which of the following is LEAST LIKELY to be a reason for a company to desire an internal audit of security controls?

subtopics.name: 6.1 Design and validate assessment, test, and audit strategies
6.2 Conduct security control testing
6.3 Collect security process data (e.g., technical and administrative)
6.4 Analyze test output and generate report
6.5 Conduct or facilitate security audits

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Impartiality

Impartiality is the least likely to be a reason for a company to desire an internal audit of security controls, as it likely wouldn't even exist. A company auditing itself lacks the credibility of putting its needs at the same level as customers. After all, it is a business trying to make money.

Expecting a business to implement cost-reducing efforts isn't unreasonable. In fact, it's exactly why companies outsource to a third party for their vulnerability assessments before a compliance check. Still, it is reasonable to have this done one way or another, usually before a mandatory quarterly audit, for example. Early knowledge of a vulnerability provides a company with more time to remediate the issue. Evolving threats would also cause a desire for internal or external audits, as threats can sometimes evolve faster than required compliance audits.

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
4.2 Secure network components
4.3 Implement secure communication channels according to design

result.explanation:
Correct answer: User Datagram Protocol (UDP)

User Datagram Protocol (UDP) is correct as it is a connectionless protocol that provides fast delivery of datagrams across a network at the transport layer.

Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is a data link layer protocol. Its job is to translate the Internet Protocol (IP) address to a Media Access Control (MAC) address. File Transfer Protocol (FTP) is an application layer protocol. It is used to put or get files onto a server. Secure Shell (SSH) is a session layer protocol that is used to encrypt sessions. Commonly used for administrative sessions to configure devices such as routers and switches.

result.prompt: Of the following, which BEST explains the rule-based access control model, especially when set up in a firewall?

subtopics.name: 5.1 Control physical and logical access to assets
5.2 Design identification and authentication strategy (e.g., people, devices, and services)
5.3 Federated identity with a third-party service
5.4 Implement and manage authorization mechanisms
5.5 Manage the identity and access provisioning lifecycle
5.6 Implement authentication systems

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Global rules are applied to all users equally

A rule-based access control model uses global rules applied to all users and other subjects equally. It does not apply rules locally or to individual users. One of the best examples today of where rule-based is applied is in firewalls. Firewalls include a set of rules or filters called Access Control Lists (ACLs), which are configured by an administrator. The firewall examines all traffic and only allows traffic that meets one of the specified rules to pass. The final rule is generally a "deny all," meaning that any remaining traffic that did not meet previous rules will be denied.

The firewall does not differentiate between users, although it can distinguish between Internet Protocol (IP) addresses or Media Access Control (MAC) addresses. Local rules can be set up for internal firewalls, but the more accurate description is that the rules are applied globally.

result.prompt: Which of the following BEST describes domain name system (DNS) poisoning?

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
4.2 Secure network components
4.3 Implement secure communication channels according to design

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Altering a DNS cache with malicious DNS records

Domain name system (DNS) cache poisoning alters a DNS cache with malicious DNS records. This causes the client to send legitimate network traffic to an attacker. For example, if an attacker modified a client's DNS cache for www.google.com to point to their malicious server, the client would visit the attacker's server, not the server for Google.

Gratuitous ARPs are a different problem. Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is used to resolve the conflict between IP (Layer 3) and MAC addresses (Layer 2).

A denial-of-service (DoS) attack shuts something down, while poisoning only involves altering the information in the records.

DNS positioning can impact connectivity, but it is a Layer 7 (application layer) threat, not a Layer 4 (transport layer) threat.

result.prompt: Which of the following might an organization's critical trade secrets be classified as?

subtopics.name: 2.1 Identify and classify information and assets
2.2 Establish information and asset handling requirements
2.3 Provision information and assets securely
2.4 Manage data lifecycle
2.5 Ensure appropriate asset retention (e.g., End of Life (EOL), End of Support)
2.6 Determine data security controls and compliance requirements

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Confidential

Private organizations can use various means of classifying their data, but some commonly used labels include:

  • Confidential or Proprietary: Highest level of classified data that could cause exceptional damage to the organization if exposed. An organization’s trade secrets or “secret sauce” could be considered proprietary data.
  • Private: Next-highest level of classified data and shouldn’t be shared outside the organization and could cause significant damage if exposed. PII and PHI may be classified as private data.
  • Sensitive: Data that could cause damage to the organization if made public. The organization’s network layout and the devices it uses may be sensitive data.
  • Public: Data that is intended to be openly disclosed. This includes the contents of websites, social media, brochures, etc.

5.6 Implement authentication systems

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Ticket-granting ticket

A Ticket-Granting Ticket (TGT) provides proof that a subject has already authenticated through a Key Distribution Center (KDC) and is authorized to request service tickets. A TGT is encrypted and can only be decrypted by the KDC. Subjects present the TGT to the KDC when requesting service tickets that provide access to other network resources.

The TGT is sent to the subject once the Kerberos Authentication Server (AS) confirms the user's claimed identity through the identification and authentication process (e.g. user identification and then a password sent to the AS).

Session keys are used to encrypt the user's session while they interact with a server. This would only protect the user's session from prying eyes, it cannot be used by the KDC to prove that they have been authenticated.

Kerberos only uses symmetric cryptography. The symmetric keys can be considered private keys, although that is confusing when one of the two keys used in asymmetric is also known as a private key. Either way, a private key cannot be used to prove authentication.

Wave pattern motion detectors send an ultrasonic or high-frequency microwave to a specific, secured area. The pattern is consistent when no object is present. When an object is present, it disrupts the wave pattern and triggers an alarm.

A mantrap is also known as a double-door system. It involves an outer door that the person can pass through after using something like a proximity card. Then there is a small area where the person is 'trapped'. To pass through the second door, they could use something like a biometric reader and a PIN. This type of system is good to place at the entrance to a data center.

A horizontal distribution system provides the connection area within the building that makes it possible to connect the cables from the data center/server room to the user's work areas. It typically includes switches and patch panels.

Proximity sensors are used to read things like smart cards. When you wave your badge/card near a reader, it is the proximity sensor that enables the reading of the card.

result.explanation:
Correct answer: Civil law

Tort law is another name for civil law. Examples include divorces and lawsuits. Civil or Tort cases occur because someone has caused harm or injury to another. That harm could be simply saying something that injures someone’s reputation (e.g. slander).

The main categories of law on the planet include but are not limited to Common law, Civil law (also known as Civilist, Napoleonic, or Roman law), Religious law, and Customary law. Common law dates back to historical England. Civil law dates back to ancient Roman times. Both civilist and common law are based on the idea that laws are created to tell people what they are not allowed to do. Once it is a law, people can be held accountable for their actions. Both common law and civilist law are broken down into three primary subcategories. 

The first subcategory is criminal law. This includes laws that make physically harming another illegal (e.g. assault and battery laws). The second subcategory is where you find lawsuits. Tort law is a good name to use here. In the US, it is commonly called civil law which causes confusion with a test like CISSP. The third subcategory is administrative (or regulatory) laws. These are laws that are intended to protect the population from corporations. Health Information Protection and Accountability Act (HIPAA) in the US is a good example here.

Religious laws are legal systems that are based on what the religion considers correct behavior. In the Middle East, Sharia law (Muslim law) is an example. Vatican City is another location where religious law is found. The pope is the head of the state because he is the head of the religion in Vatican City, which means that what is legal is up to the pope and the bible.

Customary law is also usually found in the Middle East. The customs are what is considered the law. For example, if women have never driven cars it would be illegal for them to start, simply because it has been the custom.

subtopics.name: 4.1 Apply secure design principles in network architectures
